revision.text:
{{日本の古墳 |名称 = 松面古墳 |画像 = |別名 = 元新地古墳 |所属 = [[祇園・長須賀古墳群]] |所在地 = [[千葉県]][[木更津市]]朝日2丁目 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=松面古墳}} |形状 = [[方墳]] |規模 = 44.2m×45.3m |埋葬施設 = 両袖式[[横穴式石室]] |出土品 = [[装飾付大刀]]ほか副葬品多数・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]初頭 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 方墳としては千葉県第3位
墳丘は非現存 |地図2 = {{Location map|Japan Chiba|label=松面古墳|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.png|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''松面古墳'''（まつめんこふん）は、[[千葉県]][[木更津市]]朝日にあった[[古墳]]。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 本項では、松面古墳の南にあった'''[[#塚の腰古墳|塚の腰古墳]]'''についても解説する。 == 概要 == 千葉県中部、[[小櫃川]]下流域左岸の沖積地に築造された大型方墳である。南には大溝（2号溝）を挟んで塚の腰古墳が所在した。[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に石室が発掘・調査され副葬品が出土しているほか、調査後に削平され埋没古墳となり、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、東西44.2メートル・南北45.3メートルを測り、方墳としては千葉県内で第3位の規模になる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約69.5メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約84.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。周溝からは木製品（鋤先・柄・杭・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 === 来歴 === * [[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）、開墾（または県道の土砂採取）に伴う塚の腰古墳の発掘（『千葉縣君津郡誌』上巻、『長須賀郷土史』、『木更津市史』）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 ** 出土品：土地所有者の保管後、[[1972年]]（[[昭和]]47年）に直刀以外は千葉県立上総博物館へ寄贈、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[1938年]]（昭和13年）、旧君津病院建設に伴う松面古墳の緊急調査。調査後整地（菅生遺跡調査団）{{Sfn|祇園・長須賀古墳群（千葉県の歴史 資料編 考古2）|2003}}。 ** 6月29日の人夫発掘品：木更津警察・千葉県を介して[[東京国立博物館]]が購入・保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 ** 7月19・20日の調査出土品：[[國學院大學]]へ移送・保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2005年]]度（[[平成]]17年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳の確認調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2006年]]に報告）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2010年]]度（平成22年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳・塚の腰古墳の確認調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2013年]]に報告）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2014年]]度（平成26年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳・塚の腰古墳の本調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2016年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 == 出土品 == [[ファイル:松面古墳出土 双龍環頭大刀 (J-34620).JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|双龍環頭大刀}}{{small|[[東京国立博物館]]展示。}}]] 1938年（昭和13年）の発掘による出土品は次の通り{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。人夫発掘品は木更津警察・千葉県を介して[[東京国立博物館]]が購入・保管し、調査団出土品は[[國學院大學]]へ移送・保管されており、東京国立博物館・國學院大學博物館の各所蔵品にT・Kを付して掲載する{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * 飾大刀 ** 金銅装双龍環頭大刀 1（T） ** 金銅装大刀 1（所在不明） ** 銀装捩環頭大刀柄頭 1（T） ** 金銅製鞘飾金具残片 一括（T） ** 頭椎大刀柄頭 1（所在不明） * 武器 ** 直刀 2以上（T） - 金銅製鞘飾金具残片の刀身部か。 ** 鉄鉾身・石突（K） ** 銀製弭（Kか） ** 鉄鏃（T・K） * 装飾品 ** 金銅製双魚佩 1対（T） ** 金銅製ガラス玉付木葉形腰佩 1対（K） ** 金銅製方形花形飾金具 9（K） ** ガラス小玉 - 木葉形腰佩のものか。 * 馬具 ** 金銅製鉸具付心葉形杏葉 2（T） ** 金銅装鞍磯金具 3組（T1、K2） ** 金銅製覆輪残片 6（T） ** 鉄製壺鐙残欠 1対（T） ** 鉄地金銅張革留金具 6（T） * 銅椀 1（K） * [[須恵器]] - 坏蓋3、坏身3以上、有蓋高坏5、高坏蓋4、無蓋高坏2、脚付長頸壺2、長頸壺蓋1、脚付坩片1、甕1（いずれもT）。 * [[土師器]] - 坏1、甕3（いずれもT）。 == 塚の腰古墳 == {{日本の古墳 |名称 = 塚の腰古墳 |画像 = |別名 = 塚の越古墳 |所属 = [[祇園・長須賀古墳群]] |所在地 = [[千葉県]][[木更津市]]朝日2丁目 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|3.00|N|139|56|1.00|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline|name=塚の腰古墳}} |形状 = [[方墳]] |規模 = 一辺39.5m |埋葬施設 = 不明 |出土品 = 銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]ほか |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]前半 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 墳丘は非現存 }} '''塚の腰古墳'''（つかのこしこふん、塚の越古墳）は、松面古墳の南にあった古墳。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 === 概要 === 松面古墳の南、大溝（2号溝）を挟んで築造された大型方墳である。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に発掘され副葬品が出土しているほか、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、一辺約39.5メートルを測った。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約61.0メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約73.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。埋葬施設は失われているため明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1909年（明治42年）の発掘では、副葬品として銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]などが出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]前半頃（TK217型式期）と推定される。祇園・長須賀古墳群では松面古墳に後続する首長墓と想定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 === 出土品 === 1909年（明治42年）の発掘による出土品は次の通り{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * 仿製四獣鏡 1 - 直径10.75センチメートル、約3分の1を欠く。鳥屋場1号墳出土鏡（長野県飯田市）と近似。 * 金銅製鞍磯金具 1 * 直刀 1 * 琥珀玉 1 * ガラス小玉 2 * 須恵器 - 長頸壺1。 『長須賀郷土史』によれば、鉄鏃も出土したと見られる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。以上の出土品のうち、直刀・鉄鏃を除いたものは土地所有者の保管後、千葉県立上総博物館を経て、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]で保管されている{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 == 関連施設 == * [[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]（木更津市太田） - 塚の腰古墳の出土品を保管。 * [[東京国立博物館]]（東京都台東区） - 松面古墳の出土品を保管。 * [[國學院大學博物館]]（東京都渋谷区東、國學院大學渋谷キャンパス内） - 松面古墳の出土品を保管（常設展示なし）。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * {{Cite (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 === 来歴 === * [[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）、開墾（または県道の土砂採取）に伴う塚の腰古墳の発掘（『千葉縣君津郡誌』上巻、『長須賀郷土史』、『木更津市史』）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 ** 出土品：土地所有者の保管後、[[1972年]]（[[昭和]]47年）に直刀以外は千葉県立上総博物館へ寄贈、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[1938年]]（昭和13年）、旧君津病院建設に伴う松面古墳の緊急調査。調査後整地（菅生遺跡調査団）{{Sfn|祇園・長須賀古墳群（千葉県の歴史 資料編 考古2）|2003}}。 ** 6月29日の人夫発掘品：木更津警察・千葉県を介して[[東京国立博物館]]が購入・保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 ** 7月19・20日の調査出土品：[[國學院大學]]へ移送・保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2005年]]度（[[平成]]17年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳の確認調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2006年]]に報告）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2010年]]度（平成22年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳・塚の腰古墳の確認調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2013年]]に報告）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2014年]]度（平成26年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳・塚の腰古墳の本調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2016年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 == 出土品 == [[ファイル:松面古墳出土 双龍環頭大刀 |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 墳丘は非現存 }} '''塚の腰古墳'''（つかのこしこふん、塚の越古墳）は、松面古墳の南にあった古墳。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 === 概要 === 松面古墳の南、大溝（2号溝）を挟んで築造された大型方墳である。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に発掘され副葬品が出土しているほか、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、一辺約39.5メートルを測った。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約61.0メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約73.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。埋葬施設は失われているため明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1909年（明治42年）の発掘では、副葬品として銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]などが出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]前半頃（TK217型式期）と推定される。祇園・長須賀古墳群では松面古墳に後続する首長墓と想定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 === 出土品 === 1909年（明治42年）の発掘による出土品は次の通り{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * 仿製四獣鏡 1 - 直径10.75センチメートル、約3分の1を欠く。鳥屋場1号墳出土鏡（長野県飯田市）と近似。 * 金銅製鞍磯金具 1 * 直刀 1 * 琥珀玉 1 * ガラス小玉 2 * 須恵器 - 長頸壺1。 『長須賀郷土史』によれば、鉄鏃も出土したと見られる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。以上の出土品のうち、直刀・鉄鏃を除いたものは土地所有者の保管後、千葉県立上総博物館を経て、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]で保管されている{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 == 関連施設 == * [[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]（木更津市太田） '''松面古墳'''（まつめんこふん）は、[[千葉県]][[木更津市]]朝日にあった[[古墳]]。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 本項では、松面古墳の南にあった'''[[#塚の腰古墳|塚の腰古墳]]'''についても解説する。 == 概要 == 千葉県中部、[[小櫃川]]下流域左岸の沖積地に築造された大型方墳である。南には大溝（2号溝）を挟んで塚の腰古墳が所在した。[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に石室が発掘・調査され副葬品が出土しているほか、調査後に削平され埋没古墳となり、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、東西44.2メートル・南北45.3メートルを測り、方墳としては千葉県内で第3位の規模になる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約69.5メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約84.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。周溝からは木製品（鋤先・柄・杭・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 === 来歴 === * |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 墳丘は非現存 }} '''塚の腰古墳'''（つかのこしこふん、塚の越古墳）は、松面古墳の南にあった古墳。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 === 概要 === 松面古墳の南、大溝（2号溝）を挟んで築造された大型方墳である。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に発掘され副葬品が出土しているほか、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、一辺約39.5メートルを測った。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約61.0メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約73.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。埋葬施設は失われているため明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1909年（明治42年）の発掘では、副葬品として銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]などが出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]前半頃（TK217型式期）と推定される。祇園・長須賀古墳群では松面古墳に後続する首長墓と想定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 === 出土品 === 1909年（明治42年）の発掘による出土品は次の通り{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * 仿製四獣鏡 1 - 直径10.75センチメートル、約3分の1を欠く。鳥屋場1号墳出土鏡（長野県飯田市）と近似。 * 金銅製鞍磯金具 1 * 直刀 1 * 琥珀玉 1 * ガラス小玉 2 * 須恵器 - 長頸壺1。 『長須賀郷土史』によれば、鉄鏃も出土したと見られる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。以上の出土品のうち、直刀・鉄鏃を除いたものは土地所有者の保管後、千葉県立上総博物館を経て、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]で保管されている{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 == 関連施設 == * [[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]（木更津市太田） '''松面古墳'''（まつめんこふん）は、[[千葉県]][[木更津市]]朝日にあった[[古墳]]。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 本項では、松面古墳の南にあった'''[[#塚の腰古墳|塚の腰古墳]]'''についても解説する。 == 概要 == 千葉県中部、[[小櫃川]]下流域左岸の沖積地に築造された大型方墳である。南には大溝（2号溝）を挟んで塚の腰古墳が所在した。[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に石室が発掘・調査され副葬品が出土しているほか、調査後に削平され埋没古墳となり、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、東西44.2メートル・南北45.3メートルを測り、方墳としては千葉県内で第3位の規模になる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約69.5メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約84.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。周溝からは木製品（鋤先・柄・杭・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 === 来歴 === * [[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）、開墾（または県道の土砂採取）に伴う塚の腰古墳の発掘（『千葉縣君津郡誌』上巻、『長須賀郷土史』、『木更津市史』）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 ** 出土品：土地所有者の保管後、[[1972年]]（[[昭和]]47年）に直刀以外は千葉県立上総博物館へ寄贈、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[1938年]]（昭和13年）、旧君津病院建設に伴う松面古墳の緊急調査。調査後整地（菅生遺跡調査団）{{Sfn|祇園・長須賀古墳群（千葉県の歴史 資料編 考古2）|2003}}。 ** 6月29日の人夫発掘品：木更津警察・千葉県を介して[[東京国立博物館]]が購入・保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 ** 7月19・20日の調査出土品：[[國學院大學]]へ移送・保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2005年]]度（[[平成]]17年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳の確認調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2006年]]に報告）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2010年]]度（平成22年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳・塚の腰古墳の確認調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2013年]]に報告）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2014年]]度（平成26年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳・塚の腰古墳の本調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2016年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 == 出土品 == [[ファイル:松面古墳出土 双龍環頭大刀 不明 |出土品 = 銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]ほか |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]前半 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 墳丘は非現存 }} '''塚の腰古墳'''（つかのこしこふん、塚の越古墳）は、松面古墳の南にあった古墳。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 === 概要 === 松面古墳の南、大溝（2号溝）を挟んで築造された大型方墳である。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に発掘され副葬品が出土しているほか、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、一辺約39.5メートルを測った。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約61.0メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約73.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。埋葬施設は失われているため明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1909年（明治42年）の発掘では、副葬品として銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]などが出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]前半頃（TK217型式期）と推定される。祇園・長須賀古墳群では松面古墳に後続する首長墓と想定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 === 出土品 === [[ファイル:塚の腰古墳 出土品.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|出土品}}{{small|[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]展示。}}]] 1909年（明治42年）の発掘による出土品は次の通り{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * 仿製四獣鏡 1 - 直径10.75センチメートル、約3分の1を欠く。鳥屋場1号墳出土鏡（長野県飯田市）と近似。 * 金銅製鞍磯金具 1 * 直刀 1 * 琥珀玉 1 * ガラス小玉 2 * 須恵器 - 長頸壺1。 『長須賀郷土史』によれば、鉄鏃も出土したと見られる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。以上の出土品のうち、直刀・鉄鏃を除いたものは土地所有者の保管後、千葉県立上総博物館を経て、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]で保管されている{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 '''松面古墳'''（まつめんこふん）は、[[千葉県]][[木更津市]]朝日にあった[[古墳]]。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 本項では、松面古墳の南にあった'''[[#塚の腰古墳|塚の腰古墳]]'''についても解説する。 == 概要 == 千葉県中部、[[小櫃川]]下流域左岸の沖積地に築造された大型方墳である。南には大溝（2号溝）を挟んで塚の腰古墳が所在した。[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に石室が発掘・調査され副葬品が出土しているほか、調査後に削平され埋没古墳となり、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、東西44.2メートル・南北45.3メートルを測り、方墳としては千葉県内で第3位の規模になる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約69.5メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約84.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。周溝からは木製品（鋤先・柄・杭・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 === 来歴 === * [[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）、開墾（または県道の土砂採取）に伴う塚の腰古墳の発掘（『千葉縣君津郡誌』上巻、『長須賀郷土史』、『木更津市史』）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 ** 出土品：土地所有者の保管後、[[1972年]]（[[昭和]]47年）に直刀以外は千葉県立上総博物館へ寄贈、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[1938年]]（昭和13年）、旧君津病院建設に伴う松面古墳の緊急調査。調査後整地（菅生遺跡調査団）{{Sfn|祇園・長須賀古墳群（千葉県の歴史 資料編 考古2）|2003}}。 ** 6月29日の人夫発掘品：木更津警察・千葉県を介して[[東京国立博物館]]が購入・保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 ** 7月19・20日の調査出土品：[[國學院大學]]へ移送・保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2005年]]度（[[平成]]17年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳の確認調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2006年]]に報告）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2010年]]度（平成22年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳・塚の腰古墳の確認調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2013年]]に報告）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2014年]]度（平成26年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳・塚の腰古墳の本調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2016年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 == 出土品 == [[ファイル:松面古墳出土 双龍環頭大刀 出土品.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|出土品}}{{small|[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]展示。}}]] 1909年（明治42年）の発掘による出土品は次の通り{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * 仿製四獣鏡 1 - 直径10.75センチメートル、約3分の1を欠く。鳥屋場1号墳出土鏡（長野県飯田市）と近似。 * 金銅製鞍磯金具 1 * 直刀 1 * 琥珀玉 1 * ガラス小玉 2 * 須恵器 - 長頸壺1。 『長須賀郷土史』によれば、鉄鏃も出土したと見られる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。以上の出土品のうち、直刀・鉄鏃を除いたものは土地所有者の保管後、千葉県立上総博物館を経て、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]で保管されている{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 '''松面古墳'''（まつめんこふん）は、[[千葉県]][[木更津市]]朝日にあった[[古墳]]。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 本項では、松面古墳の南にあった'''[[#塚の腰古墳|塚の腰古墳]]'''についても解説する。 == 概要 == 千葉県中部、[[小櫃川]]下流域左岸の沖積地に築造された大型方墳である。南には大溝（2号溝）を挟んで塚の腰古墳が所在した。[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に石室が発掘・調査され副葬品が出土しているほか、調査後に削平され埋没古墳となり、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、東西44.2メートル・南北45.3メートルを測り、方墳としては千葉県内で第3位の規模になる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約69.5メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約84.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。周溝からは木製品（鋤先・柄・杭・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）、開墾（または県道の土砂採取）に伴う塚の腰古墳の発掘（『千葉縣君津郡誌』上巻、『長須賀郷土史』、『木更津市史』）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 ** 出土品：土地所有者の保管後、[[1972年]]（[[昭和]]47年）に直刀以外は千葉県立上総博物館へ寄贈、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[1938年]]（昭和13年）、旧君津病院建設に伴う松面古墳の緊急調査。調査後整地（菅生遺跡調査団）{{Sfn|祇園・長須賀古墳群（千葉県の歴史 資料編 考古2）|2003}}。 ** 6月29日の人夫発掘品：木更津警察・千葉県を介して[[東京国立博物館]]が購入・保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 ** 7月19・20日の調査出土品：[[國學院大學]]へ移送・保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2005年]]度（[[平成]]17年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳の確認調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2006年]]に報告）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2010年]]度（平成22年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳・塚の腰古墳の確認調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2013年]]に報告）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[2014年]]度（平成26年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳・塚の腰古墳の本調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2016年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 == 出土品 == [[ファイル:松面古墳出土 双龍環頭大刀 {{Japanese Ancient Tombs | Name = Matsumen Kofun | Image = [[File:Matsumen Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]
跡地付近 | Alternate Name = Motoshinchi Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} | Location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}} Asahi 2-Chome | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Matsumen Kofun}} | Type = Square burial mound (方墳) | Dimensions = 44.2m×45.3m | Burial Facility = Both-sided horizontal stone chamber | Artifacts = Decorated swords, numerous burial goods, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, and sledges (修羅) | Satellite Barrows = | Construction Era = Early 7th century | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Heritage Designation = None | Cultural Property = | Special Notes = Third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture; mound no longer extant | Map2 = {{Location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} (ancient burial mound) located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. The tomb was square-shaped (方墳) and was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}. The mound has since been lost. This article also describes the '''{{ill|Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', which was located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. The Matsumoto Kofun, with a side length of approximately * {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} – Square-shaped, with a side length of approximately 44 meters. ... 6 KB (802 words) - 01:04, 15 January[[Category:original pages]][[Category:most recent 100 pages]][[Category:kofun stubs]] [[Category:Original pages]][[Category:Most recent 100 pages]] [[Category:mass bump]] [[Category:making categorization show up on newly imported categories and templates]] [[Category:松面古墳]][[ja:松面古墳]] 2025

The tomb was square-shaped (方墳) and was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}. The mound has since been lost. This article also describes the '''{{ill|Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', which was located south of Matsumen Kofun. {{Japanese Ancient Tombs | Name = Matsumen Kofun | Image = [[File:Matsumen Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]

The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{Location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} during land reclamation or roadwork (recorded in the "Kimitsu District Gazetteer," "Nagasuka Local History," and "Kisarazu City History"). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts: Initially kept by the landowner, donated to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in {{ill|1972|ja|昭和47年}} and currently housed at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}}: Emergency survey during construction of Kimitsu Hospital; tomb leveled after investigation (Sugō Site Research Group). {{Sfn|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster Historical Records|2003}} ** Artifacts discovered on June 29 were purchased by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} via the Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts unearthed on July 19–20 were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2005|ja|平成17年}}: Confirmation survey during soil improvement and removal work (reported in {{ill|2006|ja|平成18年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2010|ja|平成22年}}: Further confirmation survey (reported in {{ill|2013|ja|平成25年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2014|ja|平成26年}}: Full excavation conducted (report published in {{ill|2016|ja|平成28年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} == Artifacts == [[File:Matsumen Kofun Sword.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Twin-Dragon Ring Sword}}{{small|Exhibited at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun Ornament.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Gold-copper Fish Pendants}}{{small|Exhibited at the Tokyo National Museum.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun Sue Ware.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Sue Ware Pottery}}{{small|Exhibited at the Tokyo National Museum.}}]] Artifacts excavated in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} include: {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * Swords * Gold-copper twin-dragon ring sword (T) * Gold-copper sword (location unknown) * Silver pommel sword hilt (T) * Gold-copper sheath fittings (T) * Wooden club pommel (location unknown) * Weapons * Straight swords (two or more) (T) * Iron halberd blade and butt end (K) * Silver pommel (possibly K) * Iron arrowheads (T, K) * Ornaments * Gold-copper fish pendants (T) * Gold-copper glass-decorated leaf pendants (K) * Gold-copper floral fittings (K) * Glass beads (associated with leaf pendants) * Horse tack * Gold-copper bracketed heart-shaped pendants (T) * Gold-copper saddle fittings (T1, K2) * Gold-copper hoops (T) * Iron stirrups (T) * Iron-copper riveted fasteners (T) * Copper bowl (K) * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded cups, high-necked jars, pots (T) * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}: Bowls and jars (T) == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} (Kisarazu City) - Displays artifacts from {{ill|Matsumen Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} and {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} (Tokyo) - Stores artifacts from Matsumen Kofun. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} (Tokyo) - Stores artifacts from Matsumen Kofun (not regularly exhibited). == References == {{small|(References used for this article)}} * {{Cite book|author=Hiroshi Ozawa|year=1989|chapter=Matsumen Kofun|title={{ill|Encyclopedia of Japanese Ancient Tombs|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}|publisher={{ill|Tokyodo Publishing|ja|東京堂出版}}|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Matsumen Kofun (Ancient Tomb Encyclopedia)|1989}}}} * {{Cite book|year=1996|chapter=Matsumen Kofun|title={{ill|Topography of Chiba Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 千葉県の地名}}|publisher={{ill|Heibonsha|ja|平凡社}}|isbn=4582490085|ref={{Harvid|Matsumen Kofun (Heibonsha)|1996}}}} * {{Cite book|year=2003|chapter=Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|title=Archaeological Resources of Chiba Prefecture II|publisher=Chiba Prefecture|ref={{Harvid|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster Historical Records|2003}}}} * {{Cite book|year=2016|title=Excavation Report of Tsuka-no-Koshi and Matsumen Kofun (Vol. 13)|publisher=Kisarazu City Board of Education|ref={{Harvid|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} * {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} [[Category:Chiba Prefecture's Ancient Tombs]] [[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:Square Burial Mounds]] [[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi pages]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. pages]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} during land reclamation or roadwork (recorded in the "Kimitsu District Gazetteer," "Nagasuka Local History," and "Kisarazu City History"). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts: Initially kept by the landowner, donated to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in {{ill|1972|ja|昭和47年}} and currently housed at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}}: Emergency survey during construction of Kimitsu Hospital; tomb leveled after investigation (Sugō Site Research Group). {{Sfn|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster Historical Records|2003}} ** Artifacts discovered on June 29 were purchased by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} via the Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts unearthed on July 19–20 were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2005|ja|平成17年}}: Confirmation survey during soil improvement and removal work (reported in {{ill|2006|ja|平成18年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * pages]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). The tomb was square-shaped (方墳) and was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}. The mound has since been lost. This article also describes the '''{{ill|Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', which was located south of Matsumen Kofun. {{Infobox ancient site | name = Matsumen Kofun | image = [[File:Matsumen Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Site remains | Alias = Motoshinchi Kofun | Group = {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}} Asahi 2-Chome | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Matsumen Kofun}} | Shape = {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} | Size = 44.2m × 45.3m | Burial Facility = Dual-sleeved {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} | Artifacts = Numerous burial goods, including {{ill|Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, and {{ill|Sledges|ja|修羅 (そり)}} | Satellite Tombs = | Era = Early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Historic Site = None | Cultural Property = | Notes = Third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture
The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} during land reclamation or roadwork (recorded in the "Kimitsu District Gazetteer," "Nagasuka Local History," and "Kisarazu City History"). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts: Initially kept by the landowner, donated to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in {{ill|1972|ja|昭和47年}} and currently housed at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}}: Emergency survey during construction of Kimitsu Hospital; tomb leveled after investigation (Sugō Site Research Group). {{Sfn|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster Historical Records|2003}} ** Artifacts discovered on June 29 were purchased by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} via the Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts unearthed on July 19–20 were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2005|ja|平成17年}}: Confirmation survey during soil improvement and removal work (reported in {{ill|2006|ja|平成18年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2010|ja|平成22年}}: Further confirmation survey (reported in {{ill|2013|ja|平成25年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2014|ja|平成26年}}: Full excavation conducted (report published in {{ill|2016|ja|平成28年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} == Artifacts == [[File:Matsumen Kofun Sword.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Twin-Dragon Ring Sword}}{{small|Exhibited at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun Ornament.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Gold-copper Fish Pendants}}{{small|Exhibited at the Tokyo National Museum.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun Sue Ware.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Sue Ware Pottery}}{{small|Exhibited at the Tokyo National Museum.}}]] Artifacts excavated in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} include: {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * Swords * Gold-copper twin-dragon ring sword (T) * Gold-copper sword (location unknown) * Silver pommel sword hilt (T) * Gold-copper sheath fittings (T) * Wooden club pommel (location unknown) * Weapons * Straight swords (two or more) (T) * Iron halberd blade and butt end (K) * Silver pommel (possibly K) * Iron arrowheads (T, K) * Ornaments * Gold-copper fish pendants (T) * Gold-copper glass-decorated leaf pendants (K) * Gold-copper floral fittings (K) * Glass beads (associated with leaf pendants) * Horse tack * Gold-copper bracketed heart-shaped pendants (T) * Gold-copper saddle fittings (T1, K2) * Gold-copper hoops (T) * Iron stirrups (T) * Iron-copper riveted fasteners (T) * Copper bowl (K) * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded cups, high-necked jars, pots (T) * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}: Bowls and jars (T) == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} (Kisarazu City) - Displays artifacts from {{ill|Matsumen Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} and {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} (Tokyo) - Stores artifacts from Matsumen Kofun. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} (Tokyo) - Stores artifacts from Matsumen Kofun (not regularly exhibited). == References == {{small|(References used for this article)}} * {{Cite book|author=Hiroshi Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). The tomb was square-shaped (方墳) and was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}. The mound has since been lost. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Report|2016}} ** Artifacts: Initially kept by the landowner, donated to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in {{ill|1972|ja|昭和47年}} and currently housed at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Police and Chiba Prefecture. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts unearthed on July 19–20 were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2005|ja|平成17年}}: Confirmation survey during soil improvement and removal work (reported in {{ill|2006|ja|平成18年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear.
