== Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:pages needing attribution]][[Category:Matsumen Kofun]][[Category:pages needing attribution]] [[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. The tomb was square-shaped (方墳) and was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}. The mound has since been lost. This article also describes the '''{{ill|Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', which was located south of Matsumen Kofun. {{Infobox ancient site | name = Matsumen Kofun | image = [[File:Matsumen Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Site remains | Alias = Motoshinchi Kofun | Group = {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}} Asahi 2-Chome | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Matsumen Kofun}} | Shape = {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} | Size = 44.2m × 45.3m | Burial Facility = Dual-sleeved {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} | Artifacts = Numerous burial goods, including {{ill|Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, and {{ill|Sledges|ja|修羅 (そり)}} | Satellite Tombs = | Era = Early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Historic Site = None | Cultural Property = | Notes = Third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture
The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} during land reclamation or roadwork (recorded in the "Kimitsu District Gazetteer," "Nagasuka Local History," and "Kisarazu City History"). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts: Initially kept by the landowner, donated to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in {{ill|1972|ja|昭和47年}} and currently housed at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}}: Emergency survey during construction of Kimitsu Hospital; tomb leveled after investigation (Sugō Site Research Group). {{Sfn|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster Historical Records|2003}} ** Artifacts discovered on June 29 were purchased by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} via the Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts unearthed on July 19–20 were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2005|ja|平成17年}}: Confirmation survey during soil improvement and removal work (reported in {{ill|2006|ja|平成18年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2010|ja|平成22年}}: Further confirmation survey (reported in {{ill|2013|ja|平成25年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2014|ja|平成26年}}: Full excavation conducted (report published in {{ill|2016|ja|平成28年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} == Artifacts == [[File:Matsumen Kofun Sword.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Twin-Dragon Ring Sword}}{{small|Exhibited at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun Ornament.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Gold-copper Fish Pendants}}{{small|Exhibited at the Tokyo National Museum.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun Sue Ware.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Sue Ware Pottery}}{{small|Exhibited at the Tokyo National Museum.}}]] Artifacts excavated in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} include: {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * Swords * Gold-copper twin-dragon ring sword (T) * Gold-copper sword (location unknown) * Silver pommel sword hilt (T) * Gold-copper sheath fittings (T) * Wooden club pommel (location unknown) * Weapons * Straight swords (two or more) (T) * Iron halberd blade and butt end (K) * Silver pommel (possibly K) * Iron arrowheads (T, K) * Ornaments * Gold-copper fish pendants (T) * Gold-copper glass-decorated leaf pendants (K) * Gold-copper floral fittings (K) * Glass beads (associated with leaf pendants) * Horse tack * Gold-copper bracketed heart-shaped pendants (T) * Gold-copper saddle fittings (T1, K2) * Gold-copper hoops (T) * Iron stirrups (T) * Iron-copper riveted fasteners (T) * Copper bowl (K) * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded cups, high-necked jars, pots (T) * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}: Bowls and jars (T) == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} (Kisarazu City) - Displays artifacts from Unlinked]] [[Category:Pages needing attribution 2]][[Category:Matsumen Kofun]][[Category:Pages needing attribution 2]] [[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:Pages needing attribution 2]][[Category:Matsumen Kofun]][[Category:Pages needing attribution 2]] [[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:dd]][[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Pages needing attribution 2]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Matsumen Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Pages needing attribution 2]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). 跡地付近 | Alternate name = Motoshinchi Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}} Asahi 2-Chome | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Matsumen Kofun}} | Type = Square burial mound (方墳) | Dimensions = 44.2m×45.3m | Burial Facility = Both-sided horizontal stone chamber | Artifacts = Decorated swords, numerous burial goods, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, and sledges (修羅) | Satellite Barrows = | Construction Era = Early 7th century | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Heritage Designation = None | Cultural Property = | Special Notes = Third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture; mound no longer extant | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} (ancient burial mound) located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. The tomb was square-shaped (方墳) and was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}. The mound has since been lost. This article also describes the '''{{ill|Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', which was located south of Matsumen Kofun. {{Infobox ancient site | name = Matsumen Kofun | image = [[File:Matsumen Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Site remains | Alias = Motoshinchi Kofun | Group = {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}} Asahi 2-Chome | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Matsumen Kofun}} | Shape = {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} | Size = 44.2m × 45.3m | Burial Facility = Dual-sleeved {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} | Artifacts = Numerous burial goods, including {{ill|Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, and {{ill|Sledges|ja|修羅 (そり)}} | Satellite Tombs = | Era = Early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Historic Site = None | Cultural Property = | Notes = Third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture
The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} during land reclamation or roadwork (recorded in the "Kimitsu District Gazetteer," "Nagasuka Local History," and "Kisarazu City History"). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts: Initially kept by the landowner, donated to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in {{ill|1972|ja|昭和47年}} and currently housed at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}}: Emergency survey during construction of Kimitsu Hospital; tomb leveled after investigation (Sugō Site Research Group). {{Sfn|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster Historical Records|2003}} ** Artifacts discovered on June 29 were purchased by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} via the Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts unearthed on July 19–20 were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2005|ja|平成17年}}: Confirmation survey during soil improvement and removal work (reported in {{ill|2006|ja|平成18年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2010|ja|平成22年}}: Further confirmation survey (reported in {{ill|2013|ja|平成25年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2014|ja|平成26年}}: Full excavation conducted (report published in {{ill|2016|ja|平成28年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} == Artifacts == [[File:Matsumen Kofun Sword.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Twin-Dragon Ring Sword}}{{small|Exhibited at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun Ornament.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Gold-copper Fish Pendants}}{{small|Exhibited at the Tokyo National Museum.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun Sue Ware.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Sue Ware Pottery}}{{small|Exhibited at the Tokyo National Museum.}}]] Artifacts excavated in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} include: {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * Swords * Gold-copper twin-dragon ring sword (T) * Gold-copper sword (location unknown) * Silver pommel sword hilt (T) * Gold-copper sheath fittings (T) * Wooden club pommel (location unknown) * Weapons * Straight swords (two or more) (T) * Iron halberd blade and butt end (K) * Silver pommel (possibly K) * Iron arrowheads (T, K) * Ornaments * Gold-copper fish pendants (T) * Gold-copper glass-decorated leaf pendants (K) * Gold-copper floral fittings (K) * Glass beads (associated with leaf pendants) * Horse tack * Gold-copper bracketed heart-shaped pendants (T) * Gold-copper saddle fittings (T1, K2) * Gold-copper hoops (T) * Iron stirrups (T) * Iron-copper riveted fasteners (T) * Copper bowl (K) * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded cups, high-necked jars, pots (T) * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}: Bowls and jars (T) == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} (Kisarazu City) - Displays artifacts from {{ill|Matsumen Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} and {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} (Tokyo) - Stores artifacts from Matsumen Kofun. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} (Tokyo) - Stores artifacts from Matsumen Kofun (not regularly exhibited). == References == {{small|(References used for this article)}} * {{Cite book|author=Hiroshi The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} during land reclamation or roadwork (recorded in the "Kimitsu District Gazetteer," "Nagasuka Local History," and "Kisarazu City History"). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts: Initially kept by the landowner, donated to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in {{ill|1972|ja|昭和47年}} and currently housed at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}}: Emergency survey during construction of Kimitsu Hospital; tomb leveled after investigation (Sugō Site Research Group). {{Sfn|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster Historical Records|2003}} ** Artifacts discovered on June 29 were purchased by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} via the Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts unearthed on July 19–20 were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2005|ja|平成17年}}: Confirmation survey during soil improvement and removal work (reported in {{ill|2006|ja|平成18年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2010|ja|平成22年}}: Further confirmation survey (reported in {{ill|2013|ja|平成25年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2014|ja|平成26年}}: Full excavation conducted (report published in {{ill|2016|ja|平成28年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} == Artifacts == [[File:Matsumen Kofun Sword.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Twin-Dragon Ring Sword}}{{small|Exhibited at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun Ornament.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Gold-copper Fish Pendants}}{{small|Exhibited at the Tokyo National Museum.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun Sue Ware.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Sue Ware Pottery}}{{small|Exhibited at the Tokyo National Museum.}}]] Artifacts excavated in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} include: {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * Swords * Gold-copper twin-dragon ring sword (T) * Gold-copper sword (location unknown) * Silver pommel sword hilt (T) * Gold-copper sheath fittings (T) * Wooden club pommel (location unknown) * Weapons * Straight swords (two or more) (T) * Iron halberd blade and butt end (K) * Silver pommel (possibly K) * Iron arrowheads (T, K) * Ornaments * Gold-copper fish pendants (T) * Gold-copper glass-decorated leaf pendants (K) * Gold-copper floral fittings (K) * Glass beads (associated with leaf pendants) * Horse tack * Gold-copper bracketed heart-shaped pendants (T) * Gold-copper saddle fittings (T1, K2) * Gold-copper hoops (T) * Iron stirrups (T) * Iron-copper riveted fasteners (T) * Copper bowl (K) * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded cups, high-necked jars, pots (T) * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}: Bowls and jars (T) == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} (Kisarazu City) - Displays artifacts from {{ill|Matsumen Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} and {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} (Tokyo) - Stores artifacts from Matsumen Kofun. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} (Tokyo) - Stores artifacts from Matsumen Kofun (not regularly exhibited). == References == {{small|(References used for this article)}} * {{Cite book|author=Hiroshi [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Pages needing attribution 2]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Matsumen Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Pages needing attribution 2]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. [[Category:kk]][[Category::dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category::unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:kk]][[Category::dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category::01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} during land reclamation or roadwork (recorded in the "Kimitsu District Gazetteer," "Nagasuka Local History," and "Kisarazu City History"). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Pages needing attribution 2]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Matsumen Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Pages needing attribution 2]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Pages needing attribution]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Matsumen Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Pages needing attribution]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. The tomb was square-shaped (方墳) and was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}. The mound has since been lost. This article also describes the '''{{ill|Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', which was located south of Matsumen Kofun. {{Infobox ancient site | name = Matsumen Kofun | image = [[File:Matsumen Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]

The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi 跡地付近 | Alternate name = Motoshinchi Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}} Asahi 2-Chome | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Matsumen Kofun}} | Type = Square burial mound (方墳) | Dimensions = 44.2m×45.3m | Burial Facility = Both-sided horizontal stone chamber | Artifacts = Decorated swords, numerous burial goods, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, and sledges (修羅) | Satellite Barrows = | Construction Era = Early 7th century | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Heritage Designation = None | Cultural Property = | Special Notes = Third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture; mound no longer extant | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} (ancient burial mound) located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. The tomb was square-shaped (方墳) and was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}. The mound has since been lost. This article also describes the '''{{ill|Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', which was located south of Matsumen Kofun. {{Infobox ancient site | name = Matsumen Kofun | image = [[File:Matsumen Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Site remains | Alias = Motoshinchi Kofun | Group = {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}} Asahi 2-Chome | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Matsumen Kofun}} | Shape = {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} | Size = 44.2m × 45.3m | Burial Facility = Dual-sleeved {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} | Artifacts = Numerous burial goods, including {{ill|Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, and {{ill|Sledges|ja|修羅 (そり)}} | Satellite Tombs = | Era = Early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Historic Site = None | Cultural Property = | Notes = Third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture
The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} during land reclamation or roadwork (recorded in the "Kimitsu District Gazetteer," "Nagasuka Local History," and "Kisarazu City History"). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts: Initially kept by the landowner, donated to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in {{ill|1972|ja|昭和47年}} and currently housed at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}}: Emergency survey during construction of Kimitsu Hospital; tomb leveled after investigation (Sugō Site Research Group). {{Sfn|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster Historical Records|2003}} ** Artifacts discovered on June 29 were purchased by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} via the Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} ** Artifacts unearthed on July 19–20 were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2005|ja|平成17年}}: Confirmation survey during soil improvement and removal work (reported in {{ill|2006|ja|平成18年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2010|ja|平成22年}}: Further confirmation survey (reported in {{ill|2013|ja|平成25年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * {{ill|2014|ja|平成26年}}: Full excavation conducted (report published in {{ill|2016|ja|平成28年}}). {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} == Artifacts == [[File:Matsumen Kofun Sword.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Twin-Dragon Ring Sword}}{{small|Exhibited at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun Ornament.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Gold-copper Fish Pendants}}{{small|Exhibited at the Tokyo National Museum.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun Sue Ware.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Sue Ware Pottery}}{{small|Exhibited at the Tokyo National Museum.}}]] Artifacts excavated in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} include: {{Sfn|Matsumen Kofun Excavation Report|2016}} * Swords * Gold-copper twin-dragon ring sword (T) * Gold-copper sword (location unknown) * Silver pommel sword hilt (T) * Gold-copper sheath fittings (T) * Wooden club pommel (location unknown) * Weapons * Straight swords (two or more) (T) * Iron halberd blade and butt end (K) * Silver pommel (possibly K) * Iron arrowheads (T, K) * Ornaments * Gold-copper fish pendants (T) * Gold-copper glass-decorated leaf pendants (K) * Gold-copper floral fittings (K) * Glass beads (associated with leaf pendants) * Horse tack * Gold-copper bracketed heart-shaped pendants (T) * Gold-copper saddle fittings (T1, K2) * Gold-copper hoops (T) * Iron stirrups (T) * Iron-copper riveted fasteners (T) * Copper bowl (K) * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded cups, high-necked jars, pots (T) * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}: Bowls and jars (T) == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin-no-Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} (Kisarazu City) - Displays artifacts from {{ill|Matsumen Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} and {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} (Tokyo) - Stores artifacts from Matsumen Kofun. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == History of Investigations == * {{ill|1909|ja|明治42年}}: Excavation of {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi
