The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == 概要 == 千葉県中部、[[小櫃川]]下流域左岸の沖積地に築造された大型方墳である。南には大溝（2号溝）を挟んで塚の腰古墳が所在した。[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に石室が発掘・調査され副葬品が出土しているほか、調査後に削平され埋没古墳となり、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、東西44.2メートル・南北45.3メートルを測り、方墳としては千葉県内で第3位の規模になる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約69.5メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約84.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。周溝からは木製品（鋤先・柄・杭・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 * {{DEFAULTSORT:まつめんこふん}} 跡地付近 |別名 = 塚の越古墳 |所属 = [[祇園・長須賀古墳群]] |所在地 = [[千葉県]][[木更津市]]朝日2丁目 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|3.00|N|139|56|1.00|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline|name=塚の腰古墳}} |形状 = [[方墳]] |規模 = 一辺39.5m |埋葬施設 = 不明 |出土品 = 銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]ほか |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]前半 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 墳丘は非現存 }} '''塚の腰古墳'''（つかのこしこふん、塚の越古墳）は、松面古墳の南にあった古墳。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 === 概要 === 松面古墳の南、大溝（2号溝）を挟んで築造された大型方墳である。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に発掘され副葬品が出土しているほか、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、一辺約39.5メートルを測った。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約61.0メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約73.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。埋葬施設は失われているため明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1909年（明治42年）の発掘では、副葬品として銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]などが出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]前半頃（TK217型式期）と推定される。祇園・長須賀古墳群では松面古墳に後続する首長墓と想定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 === 出土品 === [[File:塚の腰古墳 出土品.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|出土品}}{{small|[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]展示。}}]] 1909年（明治42年）の発掘による出土品は次の通り{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * 仿製四獣鏡 1 - 直径10.75センチメートル、約3分の1を欠く。鳥屋場1号墳出土鏡（長野県飯田市）と近似。 * 金銅製鞍磯金具 1 * 直刀 1 * 琥珀玉 1 * ガラス小玉 2 * 須恵器 - 長頸壺1。 『長須賀郷土史』によれば、鉄鏃も出土したと見られる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。以上の出土品のうち、直刀・鉄鏃を除いたものは土地所有者の保管後、千葉県立上総博物館を経て、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]で保管されている{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Matsumen Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Matsumen Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == 概要 == 千葉県中部、[[小櫃川]]下流域左岸の沖積地に築造された大型方墳である。南には大溝（2号溝）を挟んで塚の腰古墳が所在した。[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に石室が発掘・調査され副葬品が出土しているほか、調査後に削平され埋没古墳となり、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、東西44.2メートル・南北45.3メートルを測り、方墳としては千葉県内で第3位の規模になる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約69.5メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約84.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。周溝からは木製品（鋤先・柄・杭・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 * {{DEFAULTSORT:まつめんこふん}} 不明 |出土品 = 銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]ほか |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]前半 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 墳丘は非現存 }} '''塚の腰古墳'''（つかのこしこふん、塚の越古墳）は、松面古墳の南にあった古墳。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 === 概要 === 松面古墳の南、大溝（2号溝）を挟んで築造された大型方墳である。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に発掘され副葬品が出土しているほか、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、一辺約39.5メートルを測った。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約61.0メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約73.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。埋葬施設は失われているため明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1909年（明治42年）の発掘では、副葬品として銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]などが出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]前半頃（TK217型式期）と推定される。祇園・長須賀古墳群では松面古墳に後続する首長墓と想定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 === 出土品 === [[File:塚の腰古墳 出土品.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|出土品}}{{small|[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]展示。}}]] 1909年（明治42年）の発掘による出土品は次の通り{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * 仿製四獣鏡 1 - 直径10.75センチメートル、約3分の1を欠く。鳥屋場1号墳出土鏡（長野県飯田市）と近似。 * 金銅製鞍磯金具 1 * 直刀 1 * 琥珀玉 1 * ガラス小玉 2 * 須恵器 - 長頸壺1。 『長須賀郷土史』によれば、鉄鏃も出土したと見られる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。以上の出土品のうち、直刀・鉄鏃を除いたものは土地所有者の保管後、千葉県立上総博物館を経て、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]で保管されている{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == 概要 == 千葉県中部、[[小櫃川]]下流域左岸の沖積地に築造された大型方墳である。南には大溝（2号溝）を挟んで塚の腰古墳が所在した。[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に石室が発掘・調査され副葬品が出土しているほか、調査後に削平され埋没古墳となり、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、東西44.2メートル・南北45.3メートルを測り、方墳としては千葉県内で第3位の規模になる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約69.5メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約84.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。周溝からは木製品（鋤先・柄・杭・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 * {{DEFAULTSORT:まつめんこふん}} 概要 === 松面古墳の南、大溝（2号溝）を挟んで築造された大型方墳である。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に発掘され副葬品が出土しているほか、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、一辺約39.5メートルを測った。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約61.0メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約73.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。埋葬施設は失われているため明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1909年（明治42年）の発掘では、副葬品として銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]などが出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]前半頃（TK217型式期）と推定される。祇園・長須賀古墳群では松面古墳に後続する首長墓と想定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 === 出土品 === [[File:塚の腰古墳 [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Site remains | Alias = Motoshinchi Kofun | Group = {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}} Asahi 2-Chome | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Matsumen Kofun}} | Shape = {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} | Size = 44.2m × 45.3m | Burial Facility = Dual-sleeved {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | Artifacts = Numerous burial goods, including {{ill|Decorated swords|ja|装飾付大刀}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, and {{ill|Sledges|ja|修羅 (そり)}} | Satellite Tombs = | Era = Early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Historic Site = None | Cultural Property = | Notes = Third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture
The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == 概要 == 千葉県中部、[[小櫃川]]下流域左岸の沖積地に築造された大型方墳である。南には大溝（2号溝）を挟んで塚の腰古墳が所在した。[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に石室が発掘・調査され副葬品が出土しているほか、調査後に削平され埋没古墳となり、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、東西44.2メートル・南北45.3メートルを測り、方墳としては千葉県内で第3位の規模になる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約69.5メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約84.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。周溝からは木製品（鋤先・柄・杭・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 * {{DEFAULTSORT:まつめんこふん}} 跡地付近 |別名 = 塚の越古墳 |所属 = [[祇園・長須賀古墳群]] |所在地 = [[千葉県]][[木更津市]]朝日2丁目 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|3.00|N|139|56|1.00|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline|name=塚の腰古墳}} |形状 = [[方墳]] |規模 = 一辺39.5m |埋葬施設 = 不明 |出土品 = 銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]ほか |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]前半 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 墳丘は非現存 }} '''塚の腰古墳'''（つかのこしこふん、塚の越古墳）は、松面古墳の南にあった古墳。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 === 概要 === 松面古墳の南、大溝（2号溝）を挟んで築造された大型方墳である。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に発掘され副葬品が出土しているほか、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、一辺約39.5メートルを測った。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約61.0メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約73.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。埋葬施設は失われているため明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1909年（明治42年）の発掘では、副葬品として銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]などが出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]前半頃（TK217型式期）と推定される。祇園・長須賀古墳群では松面古墳に後続する首長墓と想定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 === 出土品 === [[File:塚の腰古墳 出土品.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|出土品}}{{small|[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]展示。}}]] 1909年（明治42年）の発掘による出土品は次の通り{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * 仿製四獣鏡 1 - 直径10.75センチメートル、約3分の1を欠く。鳥屋場1号墳出土鏡（長野県飯田市）と近似。 * 金銅製鞍磯金具 1 * 直刀 1 * 琥珀玉 1 * ガラス小玉 2 * 須恵器 - 長頸壺1。 『長須賀郷土史』によれば、鉄鏃も出土したと見られる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。以上の出土品のうち、直刀・鉄鏃を除いたものは土地所有者の保管後、千葉県立上総博物館を経て、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]で保管されている{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Matsumen Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Matsumen Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == 概要 == 千葉県中部、[[小櫃川]]下流域左岸の沖積地に築造された大型方墳である。南には大溝（2号溝）を挟んで塚の腰古墳が所在した。[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に石室が発掘・調査され副葬品が出土しているほか、調査後に削平され埋没古墳となり、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、東西44.2メートル・南北45.3メートルを測り、方墳としては千葉県内で第3位の規模になる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約69.5メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約84.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。周溝からは木製品（鋤先・柄・杭・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 * {{DEFAULTSORT:まつめんこふん}} 不明 |出土品 = 銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]ほか |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]前半 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 墳丘は非現存 }} '''塚の腰古墳'''（つかのこしこふん、塚の越古墳）は、松面古墳の南にあった古墳。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 === 概要 === 松面古墳の南、大溝（2号溝）を挟んで築造された大型方墳である。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に発掘され副葬品が出土しているほか、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、一辺約39.5メートルを測った。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約61.0メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約73.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。埋葬施設は失われているため明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1909年（明治42年）の発掘では、副葬品として銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]などが出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]前半頃（TK217型式期）と推定される。祇園・長須賀古墳群では松面古墳に後続する首長墓と想定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 === 出土品 === [[File:塚の腰古墳 出土品.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|出土品}}{{small|[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]展示。}}]] 1909年（明治42年）の発掘による出土品は次の通り{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * 仿製四獣鏡 1 - 直径10.75センチメートル、約3分の1を欠く。鳥屋場1号墳出土鏡（長野県飯田市）と近似。 * 金銅製鞍磯金具 1 * 直刀 1 * 琥珀玉 1 * ガラス小玉 2 * 須恵器 - 長頸壺1。 『長須賀郷土史』によれば、鉄鏃も出土したと見られる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。以上の出土品のうち、直刀・鉄鏃を除いたものは土地所有者の保管後、千葉県立上総博物館を経て、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]で保管されている{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == 概要 == 千葉県中部、[[小櫃川]]下流域左岸の沖積地に築造された大型方墳である。南には大溝（2号溝）を挟んで塚の腰古墳が所在した。[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に石室が発掘・調査され副葬品が出土しているほか、調査後に削平され埋没古墳となり、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、東西44.2メートル・南北45.3メートルを測り、方墳としては千葉県内で第3位の規模になる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約69.5メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約84.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。周溝からは木製品（鋤先・柄・杭・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 * {{DEFAULTSORT:まつめんこふん}} Excavation Report|2016}} == 遺跡歴 == * [[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）、開墾（または県道の土砂採取）に伴う塚の腰古墳の発掘（『千葉縣君津郡誌』上巻、『長須賀郷土史』、『木更津市史』）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 ** 出土品：土地所有者の保管後、[[1972年]]（[[昭和]]47年）に直刀以外は千葉県立上総博物館へ寄贈、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]保管{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * [[1938年]]（昭和13年）、旧君津病院建設に伴う松面古墳の緊急調査。調査後整地（菅生遺跡調査団）{{Sfn|祇園・長須賀古墳群（千葉県の歴史 資料編 考古2）|2003}}。 [[2005年]]度（[[平成]]17年度）、土壌改良及び埋設物撤去工事に伴う松面古墳の確認調査（木更津市教育委員会、[[2006年]]に報告）{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * 跡地付近 |別名 = 塚の越古墳 |所属 = [[祇園・長須賀古墳群]] |所在地 = [[千葉県]][[木更津市]]朝日2丁目 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|3.00|N|139|56|1.00|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline|name=塚の腰古墳}} |形状 = [[方墳]] |規模 = 一辺39.5m |埋葬施設 = 不明 |出土品 = 銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]ほか |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]前半 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 墳丘は非現存 }} '''塚の腰古墳'''（つかのこしこふん、塚の越古墳）は、松面古墳の南にあった古墳。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 === 概要 === 松面古墳の南、大溝（2号溝）を挟んで築造された大型方墳である。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に発掘され副葬品が出土しているほか、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、一辺約39.5メートルを測った。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約61.0メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約73.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。埋葬施設は失われているため明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1909年（明治42年）の発掘では、副葬品として銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]などが出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]前半頃（TK217型式期）と推定される。祇園・長須賀古墳群では松面古墳に後続する首長墓と想定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 === 出土品 === [[File:塚の腰古墳 [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - The mound no longer exists | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a {{ill|Square burial mound|ja|方墳}} located in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}, {{ill|Kisarazu|ja|木更津市}}, Asahi. It was part of the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, but its mound has since disappeared. This article also discusses the nearby '''{{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''', located south of Matsumen Kofun. == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb constructed on the left bank of the alluvial plains of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. South of the tomb lay a large ditch (No. 2 ditch), beyond which {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} was located. Excavations in {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} revealed burial chambers and grave goods, followed by additional surveys in 2005, 2010, and 2014. The tomb, previously thought to be a small round mound, measured 44.2m east-to-west and 45.3m north-to-south, making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were moats and an outer ditch, encompassing 69.5m and 84.5m respectively. Artifacts such as wooden tools (plow blades, shafts, stakes, and sledges) were recovered from the moats. Notably, a {{ill|sledge|ja|修羅}} used to transport stones during tomb construction was the second of its kind discovered in Japan, following the one from {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. The burial chambers, constructed with cut soft sandstone and paved stone floors, were of the dual-sleeved horizontal stone chamber type. A sarcophagus was possibly used but remains unconfirmed. Artifacts discovered during the {{ill|1938|ja|昭和13年}} excavation included decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse tack, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb dates to the terminal {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, approximately the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 typology). Within the {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it succeeded the {{ill|Kinrei Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} and preceded {{ill|Tsuka-no-Koshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}} as the burial site of a local chief, and it is considered one of the most significant terminal Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == 概要 == 千葉県中部、[[小櫃川]]下流域左岸の沖積地に築造された大型方墳である。南には大溝（2号溝）を挟んで塚の腰古墳が所在した。[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に石室が発掘・調査され副葬品が出土しているほか、調査後に削平され埋没古墳となり、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、東西44.2メートル・南北45.3メートルを測り、方墳としては千葉県内で第3位の規模になる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約69.5メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約84.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。周溝からは木製品（鋤先・柄・杭・[[修羅 (そり)|修羅]]・刀形など）が出土しており、特に修羅は古墳築造に際して石材を運搬するもので、[[三ツ塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]）に次ぐ国内2例目として注目される。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]。石室の石材は軟質砂岩の切石で、床面は板石敷であったという{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。病院に伝わった石棺が使用された可能性があるが、他の記録には記載がなく明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1938年（昭和13年）の発掘では、石室内から[[装飾付大刀]]・武器・装飾品・馬具・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]]など多数の副葬品が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]初頭頃（TK209型式期）と推定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。祇園・長須賀古墳群では[[金鈴塚古墳]]（木更津市長須賀）に後続し、塚の腰古墳に先行する首長墓と想定され、房総では代表的な終末期古墳の1つとして重要視される古墳になる。 * {{DEFAULTSORT:まつめんこふん}} 跡地付近 |別名 = 塚の越古墳 |所属 = [[祇園・長須賀古墳群]] |所在地 = [[千葉県]][[木更津市]]朝日2丁目 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|3.00|N|139|56|1.00|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline|name=塚の腰古墳}} |形状 = [[方墳]] |規模 = 一辺39.5m |埋葬施設 = 不明 |出土品 = 銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]ほか |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]前半 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 墳丘は非現存 }} '''塚の腰古墳'''（つかのこしこふん、塚の越古墳）は、松面古墳の南にあった古墳。形状は[[方墳]]。[[祇園・長須賀古墳群]]を構成した古墳の1つ。現在では墳丘は失われている。 === 概要 === 松面古墳の南、大溝（2号溝）を挟んで築造された大型方墳である。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に発掘され副葬品が出土しているほか、[[2005年|2005]]・[[2010年|2010]]・[[2014年]]度（[[平成]]17・22・26年度）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で（調査前は小円墳とされた）、一辺約39.5メートルを測った。墳丘周囲には周溝・外周溝が巡らされており、周溝を含んだ規模は約61.0メートル、外周溝を含んだ規模は約73.5メートルにおよぶ{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。埋葬施設は失われているため明らかでない{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。1909年（明治42年）の発掘では、副葬品として銅鏡・直刀・鉄鏃・馬具・[[須恵器]]などが出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]前半頃（TK217型式期）と推定される。祇園・長須賀古墳群では松面古墳に後続する首長墓と想定される{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 === 出土品 === [[File:塚の腰古墳 出土品.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|出土品}}{{small|[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]展示。}}]] 1909年（明治42年）の発掘による出土品は次の通り{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 * 仿製四獣鏡 1 - 直径10.75センチメートル、約3分の1を欠く。鳥屋場1号墳出土鏡（長野県飯田市）と近似。 * 金銅製鞍磯金具 1 * 直刀 1 * 琥珀玉 1 * ガラス小玉 2 * 須恵器 - 長頸壺1。 『長須賀郷土史』によれば、鉄鏃も出土したと見られる{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。以上の出土品のうち、直刀・鉄鏃を除いたものは土地所有者の保管後、千葉県立上総博物館を経て、現在は[[木更津市郷土博物館金のすず]]で保管されている{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}。 [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] == Overview == Matsumen Kofun was a large square tomb built in the alluvial plains along the left bank of the {{ill|Obitsu River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To its south, across a large trench (2nd Trench), lay the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. The tomb was excavated in [[1938]] ({{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和時代}} 13), yielding burial goods. After the excavation, the mound was leveled and buried. Subsequent excavations were conducted in [[2005]], [[2010]], and [[2014]]. The mound measured 44.2m (east-west) by 45.3m (north-south), making it the third-largest square tomb in Chiba Prefecture. Surrounding the mound were a moat and an outer moat. Including these, the dimensions reached approximately 69.5m with the moat and 84.5m with the outer moat. Artifacts such as wooden tools (spade blades, handles, stakes, sledges, sword-shaped implements) were recovered from the moat. The sledge, used to transport stones for construction, was the second such find in Japan after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} in Osaka Prefecture. The burial facility was a both-sided horizontal stone chamber constructed from soft sandstone blocks, with a floor paved with slabs. Although a stone coffin was reportedly transferred to a hospital, its existence is not confirmed in other records. Excavation in [[1938]] yielded numerous burial goods, including decorated swords, weapons, ornaments, horse gear, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The tomb is dated to the early [[7th century]] (TK209 phase) during the terminal phase of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}. Matsumen Kofun succeeded the {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} in the Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster and preceded the Tsukanokoshi Kofun as a burial site for regional leaders. It is considered an important example of terminal-phase kofun in the Bōsō Peninsula. == Artifact History == * [[1909]] ({{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}} 42): Excavation of Tsukanokoshi Kofun during land development or road construction (documented in *Chiba Prefecture Kimitsu District Chronicles* and *Nagasuka Local History*). ** Artifacts were initially kept by the landowner and later donated (excluding swords) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum in [[1972]] (Showa 47). They are now housed in the {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}. * [[1938]]: Emergency survey of Matsumen Kofun during the construction of the former Kimitsu Hospital. The site was leveled after the survey. ** June 29: Finds by laborers were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}. ** July 19–20: Artifacts discovered during the formal survey were transferred to {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}. * [[2005]], [[2010]], [[2014]]: Subsequent excavations revealed additional findings, documented in reports by the Kisarazu City Board of Education. == Artifacts == {{Gallery | File:Matsumen Kofun, sword.jpg|Decorated sword with twin dragons | File:Matsumen Kofun, fish pendant.jpg|Gold-copper fish-shaped pendant | File:Matsumen Kofun, sue ware.jpg|Sue ware jar }} Artifacts from the [[1938]] excavation include: * Decorated swords: * Gold-copper twin-dragon sword (1) * Other decorated swords (lost) * Hilt ends and fragments * Weapons: * Iron swords (2+) * Iron spearheads * Ornaments: * Gold-copper fish-shaped pendants (1 pair) * Beads * Horse gear: * Bits and decorative fittings * Ceramics: * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}: Lidded bowls, tall-necked jars, etc. * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Folk Museum Kin no Suzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} - Houses artifacts from Matsumen and Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} - Preserves Matsumen Kofun artifacts. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} - Holds Matsumen Kofun artifacts. == See Also == * {{ill|Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} * {{ill|Kinreitsuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Ancient tombs in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:History of Kisarazu]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square burial mounds]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Matsumen Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Matsumen Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:松面古墳]] * [[Gion-Nagasuka Kofun Cluster]] ...n in the early 7th century, square kofun like the {{ill|Matsumoto Kofun|ja|松面古墳}} began to appear. Vicinity of the site |Alternate name = Former Shinchi Kofun |Affiliation = {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} |Location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu City|ja|木更津市}} Asahi 2‐chome |Coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=松面古墳}} |Shape = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳}} |Scale = 44.2m×45.3m |Burial facility = Two‐sleeve style {{ill|Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} |Excavated items = {{ill|Decorated Sword|ja|装飾付大刀}} and numerous other burial goods, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, and {{ill|Shura|ja|修羅 (そり)|lt=Shura|lt_ja=修羅}} |Attached mound = |Construction period = Early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Interred = |Mausoleum = |Historic site = None |Tangible Cultural Property = |Special notes = Ranked as the third‐largest square kofun in Chiba Prefecture
The tumulus is no longer extant |Map 2 = {{Location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=Square Kofun.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a burial mound (kofun) located in Asahi, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu City|ja|木更津市}}. Its shape was that of a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳}}. It was one of the kofun comprising the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}. The tumulus is now lost. In this article the mound located to the south of Matsumen Kofun – '''{{ill|Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳}}''' – is also explained. == Overview == It is a large square kofun built on the alluvial plain along the left bank of the lower reaches of the {{ill|Kobiki River|ja|小櫃川}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To the south, separated by a large moat (Moat No.2), stood the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. In {{ill|1938|ja|1938年}} (the 13th year of the {{ill|Showa era|ja|昭和}}), its stone chamber was excavated and investigated and burial goods were unearthed; later, after being leveled and becoming a buried mound, excavation surveys were carried out in {{ill|2005|ja|2005年|lt=2005}}, {{ill|2010|ja|2010年|lt=2010}}, and {{ill|2014|ja|2014年}} (in the 17th, 22nd, and 26th fiscal years of the {{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成}}). The tumulus was square in shape (previously regarded as a small circular mound before investigation), measuring 44.2 meters east–west and 45.3 meters north–south – making it the third largest square kofun in Chiba Prefecture{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Around the mound, both a peripheral moat and an outer moat encircled the site; including the peripheral moat, the overall scale was approximately 69.5 meters, and including the outer moat, about 84.5 meters{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. From the peripheral moat were unearthed wooden objects – such as plowshares, handles, stakes, {{ill|Shura|ja|修羅 (そり)|lt=Shura|lt_ja=修羅}}, and sword‐like items – and notably the Shura, used for transporting stone during construction, is noteworthy as only the second example in the country after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳}} (in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}/{{ill|Fujiidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}). The burial facility was the two‐sleeve style {{ill|Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}. Its stone chamber was constructed from cut soft sandstone with a flagstone floor, according to reports{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Although there is a possibility that a stone coffin passed on to a hospital was used, no other records mention this, leaving it unclear{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The 1938 excavation (13th year of the Showa era) unearthed numerous burial goods from within the stone chamber – including the {{ill|Decorated Sword|ja|装飾付大刀}}, various weapons, ornaments, horse fittings, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}. The construction period is estimated to be in the early {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK209 period) of the Late Kofun period{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Within the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it is thought to have succeeded the {{ill|Kanazurizuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳}} (in {{ill|Kisarazu City Nagasuka|ja|木更津市長須賀}}) and is assumed to be a chieftain tomb preceding the Tsukanokoshi Kofun – making it one of the representative Late Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == Archaeological History == * In {{ill|1909|ja|1909年}} (42nd year of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}}), the Tsukanokoshi Kofun was excavated during land reclamation (or soil removal for a prefectural road) – as recorded in the Chiba Prefecture Kunitsu County Gazette (Volume 1), Nagasuka Local History, and Kisarazu City History{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. ** Excavated items: After being retained by the landowner, all items except for the straight sword were donated in {{ill|1972|ja|1972年}} (47th year of the {{ill|Showa era|ja|昭和}}) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum, and are now preserved at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938年}} (13th year of the Showa era), an emergency survey of the Matsumen Kofun was conducted in connection with the construction of the former Kunitsu Hospital; the site was leveled after the survey (by the Suga Archaeological Survey Group){{Sfn|祇園・長須賀古墳群（千葉県の歴史 資料編 考古2）|2003}}. ** The manual excavation on June 29 – the excavated items were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} through Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. ** The items excavated during the survey on July 19–20 were transferred to and preserved at {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In the fiscal year of {{ill|2005|ja|2005年}} (17th fiscal year of the {{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成}}), a verification survey of Matsumen Kofun was conducted in connection with soil improvement and the removal of buried objects (by the Kisarazu City Board of Education, reported in {{ill|2006|ja|2006年}}){{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In the fiscal year of {{ill|2010|ja|2010年}} (22nd fiscal year of the {{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成}}), a verification survey of both Matsumen Kofun and Tsukanokoshi Kofun was carried out in connection with soil improvement and the removal of buried objects (by the Kisarazu City Board of Education, reported in {{ill|2013|ja|2013年}}){{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In the fiscal year of {{ill|2014|ja|2014年}} (26th fiscal year of the {{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成}}), a full-scale survey of both Matsumen Kofun and Tsukanokoshi Kofun was conducted in connection with soil improvement and the removal of buried objects (by the Kisarazu City Board of Education, with the report published in {{ill|2016|ja|2016年}}){{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. == Excavated Items == [[File:Matsumen Kofun 出土 双龍環頭大刀 (J-34620).JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Double Dragon Ring‐Headed Sword}}{{small|{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} display.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun 出土 金銅製魚佩 (J-34624).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Bronze Fish‐shaped Ornament}}{{small|{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} display.}}]] [[File:Matsumen Kofun 出土 須恵器 甕 (J-34611).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Sue Ware Jar}}{{small|{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} display.}}]] The items excavated during the 1938 excavation (13th year of the Showa era) are as follows{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The manual excavation items were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} through Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture, while the items unearthed by the survey team were transferred to and preserved at {{ill|Kokugakuin University|ja|國學院大學}}; the collections at both the Tokyo National Museum and the Kokugakuin University Museum are labeled with T and K respectively{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * Decorated Sword ** Bronze‐adorned Double Dragon Ring‐Headed Sword, 1 (T) ** Bronze‐adorned Sword, 1 (location unknown) ** Silver‐adorned Twisted Ring‐Headed Sword Hilt, 1 (T) ** Bronze‐made Sword Scabbard Ornament Fragment, collectively (T) ** Skull‐shaped Sword Hilt, 1 (location unknown) * Weapons ** Straight Sword, 2 or more (T) – possibly the blade portion of the bronze scabbard ornament fragment ** Iron halberd shaft and stone tip (K) ** Silver‐made dagger (possibly K) ** Iron arrowheads (T, K) * Ornaments ** Bronze‐made Double Fish‐shaped Pendant, 1 pair (T) ** Bronze‐made Glass Bead‐attached Leaf‐shaped Waist Ornament, 1 pair (K) ** Bronze‐made Square Floral‐shaped Ornaments, 9 (K) ** Small glass beads – possibly from the leaf‐shaped waist ornament * Horse Fittings ** Bronze‐made Heart‐shaped Apricot Leaf with hinge, 2 (T) ** Bronze‐adorned saddle and stirrup fittings, 3 sets (T1, K2) ** Bronze‐made remnants of a covered wheel, 6 (T) ** Incomplete iron spurred stirrup, 1 pair (T) ** Iron‐based bronze leather fastening fittings, 6 (T) * Bronze bowl, 1 (K) * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} – 3 broken lids, 3 or more broken bodies; 5 high broken jars with lids, 4 high broken jars with lids, 2 high broken jars without lids, 2 long‐necked jars with feet, 1 long‐necked jar with lid, 1 footed crucible, 1 jar (all T) * {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} – 1 broken vessel, 3 jars (all T) == Tsukanokoshi Kofun == {{Japanese Kofun |Name = Tsukanokoshi Kofun |Image = [[File:Tsukanokoshi Kofun (Kisarazu), gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Vicinity of the site |Alternate name = Tsukanokoshi Kofun |Affiliation = {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}} |Location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県}}{{ill|Kisarazu City|ja|木更津市}} Asahi 2‐chome |Coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|3.00|N|139|56|1.00|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline|name=塚の腰古墳}} |Shape = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳}} |Scale = 39.5 m on each side |Burial facility = Unknown |Excavated items = Bronze mirror, straight sword, iron arrowheads, horse fittings, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, among others |Attached mound = |Construction period = First half of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Interred = |Mausoleum = |Historic site = None |Tangible Cultural Property = |Special notes = The tumulus is no longer extant }} '''Tsukanokoshi Kofun''' (塚の腰古墳) was a burial mound located to the south of Matsumen Kofun. Its shape was that of a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳}}. It was one of the kofun comprising the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}. The tumulus is now lost. === Overview === It is a large square kofun constructed to the south of Matsumen Kofun, separated by a large moat (Moat No.2). It was excavated in {{ill|1909|ja|1909年}} (42nd year of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}}), during which burial goods were unearthed, and further excavation surveys were conducted in the fiscal years of {{ill|2005|ja|2005年|lt=2005}}, {{ill|2010|ja|2010年|lt=2010}}, and {{ill|2014|ja|2014年}} (17th, 22nd, and 26th fiscal years of the {{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成}}). The tumulus was square in shape (previously considered a small circular mound before investigation), with each side measuring approximately 39.5 meters. Around the mound were both a peripheral moat and an outer moat; including the peripheral moat, the overall scale was about 61.0 meters, and including the outer moat, about 73.5 meters{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. As the burial facility has been lost, its details remain unknown{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The 1909 excavation (42nd year of the Meiji era) unearthed burial goods including a bronze mirror, a straight sword, iron arrowheads, horse fittings, and {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, among others. The construction period is estimated to be in the first half of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} (TK217 period) of the Late Kofun period. Within the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群}}, it is assumed to be a chieftain tomb succeeding Matsumen Kofun{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. === Excavated Items === [[File:塚の腰古墳 出土品.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Excavated Items}}{{small|Displayed at {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}.}}]] The excavated items from the 1909 excavation (42nd year of the Meiji era) are as follows{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}: * Replica Four‐Animal Mirror, 1 – Diameter 10.75 cm, missing about one–third; similar to the mirror unearthed from Toriya‐baja Kofun No.1 (in Iida, Nagano Prefecture) * Bronze‐made Saddle and Stirrup Fitting, 1 * Straight Sword, 1 * Amber Bead, 1 * Small Glass Beads, 2 * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} – 1 long–necked jar According to Nagasuka Local History, iron arrowheads are also believed to have been unearthed{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Of the above items, all except the straight sword and iron arrowheads were retained by the landowner, then passed to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum, and are now preserved at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}}{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず}} (Ōta, Kisarazu City) – Preserves the excavated items from Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}} (Taitō, Tokyo) – Preserves the excavated items from Matsumen Kofun. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館}} (Higashi, Shibuya, Tokyo; located within the Kokugakuin University Shibuya Campus) – Preserves the excavated items from Matsumen Kofun (not on permanent display). == Footnotes ==
