This was added through to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Japanese Kofun |name = Matsumen Kofun |image = [[File:Matsumen Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Vicinity of the site |alternate_name = Former Shinchi Kofun |part_of = {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}} |location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|Kisarazu|en|Kisarazu|WD=Q335427|lt=Kisarazu City}} Asahi 2‐chome |coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=松面古墳}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_size = 44.2m×45.3m |burial = Two‐sleeve style {{ill|Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} |excavations = {{ill|Decorated Sword|ja|装飾付大刀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decorated Sword|1=decorated swords|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48749737}} and numerous other burial goods, {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}}, and {{ill|Shura|ja|修羅 (そり)|lt=Shura|lt_ja=修羅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shura|1=Shura (sled)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11386350}} |Attached mound = |built = Early {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} |Interred = |Mausoleum = |Historic Site = None |Tangible Cultural Property = |notes = Ranked as the third‐largest square kofun in Chiba Prefecture
The tumulus is no longer extant |map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=Square Kofun.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a Kofun (kofun) located in Asahi, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|Kisarazu|en|Kisarazu|WD=Q335427|lt=Kisarazu City}}. Its type was that of a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. It was one of the kofun comprising the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}. The tumulus is now lost. In this article the mound located to the south of Matsumen Kofun – '''{{ill|Matsumen Kofun|lt=Matsumen Kofun|lt=Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 松面古墳}}''' – is also explained. == Overview == It is a large square kofun built on the alluvial plain along the left bank of the lower reaches of the {{ill|Obitsu River|en|Obitsu River|WD=Q7074982|lt=Kobiki River}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To the south, separated by a large moat (Moat No.2), stood the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. In {{ill|1938|en|1938|WD=Q18645|lt=1938}} (the 13th year of the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Showa era}}), its stone chamber was excavated and investigated and burial goods were unearthed; later, after being leveled and becoming a buried mound, excavation surveys were carried out in {{ill|2005|en|2005|WD=Q2019|lt=2005}}, {{ill|2010|en|2010|WD=Q1995|lt=2010}}, and {{ill|2014|en|2014|WD=Q1999|lt=2014}} (in the 17th, 22nd, and 26th fiscal years of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}). The tumulus was square in type (previously regarded as a small circular mound before investigation), measuring 44.2 meters east–west and 45.3 meters north–south – making it the third largest square kofun in Chiba Prefecture{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Around the mound, both a peripheral moat and an outer moat encircled the site; including the peripheral moat, the overall map_size was approximately 69.5 meters, and including the outer moat, about 84.5 meters{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. From the peripheral moat were unearthed wooden objects – such as plowshares, handles, stakes, {{ill|Shura|ja|修羅 (そり)|lt=Shura|lt_ja=修羅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shura|1=Shura (sled)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11386350}}, and sword‐like items – and notably the Shura, used for transporting stone during construction, is noteworthy as only the second example in the country after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitsuzuka Kofun|qq=}} (in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}/{{ill|Fujiidera|en|Fujiidera|WD=Q634011|lt=Fujiidera City}}). The burial facility was the two‐sleeve style {{ill|Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}. Its stone chamber was constructed from cut soft sandstone with a flagstone floor, according to reports{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Although there is a possibility that a Sarcophagus passed on to a hospital was used, no other records mention this, leaving it unclear{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The 1938 excavation (13th year of the Showa era) unearthed numerous burial goods from within the stone chamber – including the {{ill|Decorated Sword|ja|装飾付大刀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decorated Sword|1=decorated swords|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48749737}}, various weapons, ornaments, horse fittings, {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, and {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}}. The construction period is estimated to be in the early {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} (TK209 period) of the Late Kofun period{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Within the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}, it is thought to have succeeded the {{ill|Kanazurizuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳|1=Kinreizuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanazurizuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinreizuka Kofun|qq=}} (in {{ill|Kisarazu City Nagasuka|ja|木更津市長須賀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Nagasuka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) and is assumed to be a chieftain tomb preceding the Tsukanokoshi Kofun – making it one of the representative Late Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == Archaeological History == * In {{ill|1909|en|1909|WD=Q2057|lt=1909}} (42nd year of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}), the Tsukanokoshi Kofun was excavated during land reclamation (or soil removal for a prefectural road) – as recorded in the Chiba Prefecture Kunitsu County Gazette (Volume 1), Nagasuka Local History, and Kisarazu City The manual excavation items were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} through Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture, while the items unearthed by the survey team were transferred to and preserved at {{ill|Kokugakuin University|en|Kokugakuin University|WD=Q495330|lt=Kokugakuin University}}; the collections at both the Tokyo National Museum and the Kokugakuin University Museum are labeled with T and K respectively{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * Decorated Sword ** Bronze‐adorned Double Dragon Ring‐Headed Sword, 1 (T) ** Bronze‐adorned Sword, 1 (location unknown) ** Silver‐adorned Twisted Ring‐Headed Sword Hilt, 1 (T) ** Bronze‐made Sword Scabbard Ornament Fragment, collectively (T) ** Skull‐shaped Sword Hilt, 1 (location unknown) * Weapons ** Straight Sword, 2 or more (T) – possibly the blade portion of the bronze scabbard ornament fragment ** Iron halberd shaft and stone tip (K) ** Silver‐made dagger (possibly K) ** Iron arrowheads (T, K) * Ornaments ** Bronze‐made Double Fish‐shaped Pendant, 1 pair (T) ** Bronze‐made Glass Bead‐attached Leaf‐shaped Waist Ornament, 1 pair (K) ** Bronze‐made Square Floral‐shaped Ornaments, 9 (K) ** Small glass beads – possibly from the leaf‐shaped waist ornament * Horse Fittings ** Bronze‐made Heart‐shaped Apricot Leaf with hinge, 2 (T) ** Bronze‐adorned saddle and stirrup fittings, 3 sets (T1, K2) ** Bronze‐made remnants of a covered wheel, 6 (T) ** Incomplete iron spurred stirrup, 1 pair (T) ** Iron‐based bronze leather fastening fittings, 6 (T) * Bronze bowl, 1 (K) * {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} – 3 broken lids, 3 or more broken bodies; 5 high broken jars with lids, 4 high broken jars with lids, 2 high broken jars without lids, 2 long‐necked jars with feet, 1 long‐necked jar with lid, 1 footed crucible, 1 jar (all T) * {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}} – 1 broken vessel, 3 jars (all T) == Tsukanokoshi Kofun == {{Japanese Kofun |name = Tsukanokoshi Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukanokoshi Kofun (Kisarazu), gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Vicinity of the site |alternate_name = Tsukanokoshi Kofun |part_of = {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}} |location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|Kisarazu|en|Kisarazu|WD=Q335427|lt=Kisarazu City}} Asahi 2‐chome |coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|3.00|N|139|56|1.00|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline|name=塚の腰古墳}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_size = 39.5 m on each side |burial = Unknown |excavations = Bronze mirror, straight sword, iron arrowheads, horse fittings, {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, among others |Attached mound = |built = First half of the {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} |Interred = |Mausoleum = |Historic Site = None |Tangible Cultural Property = |notes = The tumulus is no longer extant }} '''Tsukanokoshi Kofun''' (塚の腰古墳) was a Kofun located to the south of Matsumen Kofun. Its type was that of a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. It was one of the kofun comprising the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}. The tumulus is now lost. == Overview == It is a large square kofun constructed to the south of Matsumen Kofun, separated by a large moat (Moat No.2). It was excavated in {{ill|1909|en|1909|WD=Q2057|lt=1909}} (42nd year of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}), during which burial goods were unearthed, and further excavation surveys were conducted in the fiscal years of {{ill|2005|en|2005|WD=Q2019|lt=2005}}, {{ill|2010|en|2010|WD=Q1995|lt=2010}}, and {{ill|2014|en|2014|WD=Q1999|lt=2014}} (17th, 22nd, and 26th fiscal years of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}). The tumulus was square in type (previously considered a small circular mound before investigation), with each side measuring approximately 39.5 meters. Around the mound were both a peripheral moat and an outer moat; including the peripheral moat, the overall map_size was about 61.0 meters, and including the outer moat, about 73.5 meters{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. As the burial facility has been lost, its details remain unknown{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The 1909 excavation (42nd year of the Meiji era) unearthed burial goods including a bronze mirror, a straight sword, iron arrowheads, horse fittings, and {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, among others. The construction period is estimated to be in the first half of the {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} (TK217 period) of the Late Kofun period. Within the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}, it is assumed to be a chieftain tomb succeeding Matsumen Kofun{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. === Excavated Items === [[File:塚の腰古墳 出土品.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Excavated Items}}{{small|Displayed at {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|1=Kisarazu Hometown Museum Kin-no-Suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91380712}}.}}]] The burial goods from the 1909 excavation (42nd year of the Meiji era) are as follows{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}: * Replica Four‐Animal Mirror, 1 – Diameter 10.75 cm, missing about one–third; similar to the mirror unearthed from Toriya‐baja Kofun No.1 (in Iida, Nagano Prefecture) * Bronze‐made Saddle and Stirrup Fitting, 1 * Straight Sword, 1 * Amber Bead, 1 * Small Glass Beads, 2 * {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} – 1 long–necked jar According to Nagasuka Local History, iron arrowheads are also believed to have been unearthed{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The tumulus is no longer extant |map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=Square Kofun.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a Kofun (kofun) located in Asahi, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|Kisarazu|en|Kisarazu|WD=Q335427|lt=Kisarazu City}}. Its type was that of a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. It was one of the kofun comprising the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}. The tumulus is now lost. In this article the mound located to the south of Matsumen Kofun – '''{{ill|Matsumen Kofun|lt=Matsumen Kofun|lt=Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 松面古墳}}''' – is also explained. == Overview == It is a large square kofun built on the alluvial plain along the left bank of the lower reaches of the {{ill|Obitsu River|en|Obitsu River|WD=Q7074982|lt=Kobiki River}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To the south, separated by a large moat (Moat No.2), stood the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. In {{ill|1938|en|1938|WD=Q18645|lt=1938}} (the 13th year of the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Showa era}}), its stone chamber was excavated and investigated and burial goods were unearthed; later, after being leveled and becoming a buried mound, excavation surveys were carried out in {{ill|2005|en|2005|WD=Q2019|lt=2005}}, {{ill|2010|en|2010|WD=Q1995|lt=2010}}, and {{ill|2014|en|2014|WD=Q1999|lt=2014}} (in the 17th, 22nd, and 26th fiscal years of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}). The tumulus was square in type (previously regarded as a small circular mound before investigation), measuring 44.2 meters east–west and 45.3 meters north–south – making it the third largest square kofun in Chiba Prefecture{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Around the mound, both a peripheral moat and an outer moat encircled the site; including the peripheral moat, the overall map_size was approximately 69.5 meters, and including the outer moat, about 84.5 meters{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. From the peripheral moat were unearthed wooden objects – such as plowshares, handles, stakes, {{ill|Shura|ja|修羅 (そり)|lt=Shura|lt_ja=修羅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shura|1=Shura (sled)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11386350}}, and sword‐like items – and notably the Shura, used for transporting stone during construction, is noteworthy as only the second example in the country after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitsuzuka Kofun|qq=}} (in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}/{{ill|Fujiidera|en|Fujiidera|WD=Q634011|lt=Fujiidera City}}). The burial facility was the two‐sleeve style {{ill|Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}. Its stone chamber was constructed from cut soft sandstone with a flagstone floor, according to reports{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Although there is a possibility that a Sarcophagus passed on to a hospital was used, no other records mention this, leaving it unclear{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The 1938 excavation (13th year of the Showa era) unearthed numerous burial goods from within the stone chamber – including the {{ill|Decorated Sword|ja|装飾付大刀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decorated Sword|1=decorated swords|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48749737}}, various weapons, ornaments, horse fittings, {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, and {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}}. The construction period is estimated to be in the early {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} (TK209 period) of the Late Kofun period{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Within the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}, it is thought to have succeeded the {{ill|Kanazurizuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳|1=Kinreizuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanazurizuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinreizuka Kofun|qq=}} (in {{ill|Kisarazu City Nagasuka|ja|木更津市長須賀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Nagasuka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) and is assumed to be a chieftain tomb preceding the Tsukanokoshi Kofun – making it one of the representative Late Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == Archaeological History == * In {{ill|1909|en|1909|WD=Q2057|lt=1909}} (42nd year of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}), the Tsukanokoshi Kofun was excavated during land reclamation (or soil removal for a prefectural road) – as recorded in the Chiba Prefecture Kunitsu County Gazette (Volume 1), Nagasuka Local History, and Kisarazu City History{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. ** excavations: After being retained by the landowner, all items except for the straight sword were donated in {{ill|1972|en|1972|WD=Q2476|lt=1972}} (47th year of the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Showa era}}) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum, and are now preserved at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|1=Kisarazu Hometown Museum Kin-no-Suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91380712}}{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In {{ill|1938|en|1938|WD=Q18645|lt=1938}} (13th year of the Showa era), an emergency survey of the Matsumen Kofun was conducted in connection with the construction of the former Kunitsu Hospital; the site was leveled after the survey (by the Suga Archaeological Survey Group){{Sfn|祇園・長須賀古墳群（千葉県の歴史 資料編 考古2）|2003}}. ** The manual excavation on June 29 – the burial goods were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} through Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. ** The items excavated during the survey on July 19–20 were transferred to and preserved at {{ill|Kokugakuin University|en|Kokugakuin University|WD=Q495330|lt=Kokugakuin University}}{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In the fiscal year of {{ill|2005|en|2005|WD=Q2019|lt=2005}} (17th fiscal year of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}), a verification survey of Matsumen Kofun was conducted in connection with soil improvement and the removal of buried objects (by the Kisarazu City Board of Education, reported in {{ill|2006|en|2006|WD=Q2021|lt=2006}}){{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In the fiscal year of {{ill|2010|en|2010|WD=Q1995|lt=2010}} (22nd fiscal year of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}), a verification survey of both Matsumen Kofun and Tsukanokoshi Kofun was carried out in connection with soil improvement and the removal of buried objects (by the Kisarazu City Board of Education, reported in {{ill|2013|en|2013|WD=Q1998|lt=2013}}){{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In the fiscal year of {{ill|2014|en|2014|WD=Q1999|lt=2014}} (26th fiscal year of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}), a full-map_size survey of both Matsumen Kofun and Tsukanokoshi Kofun was conducted in connection with soil improvement and the removal of buried objects (by the Kisarazu City Board of Education, with the report published in {{ill|2016|en|2016|WD=Q25245|lt=2016}}){{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. == Excavated Items == [[File:松面古墳出土 双龍環頭大刀 (J-34620).JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Double Dragon Ring‐Headed Sword}}{{small|{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} display.}}]] [[File:松面古墳出土 金銅製魚佩 (J-34624).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Bronze Fish‐shaped Ornament}}{{small|{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} display.}}]] [[File:松面古墳出土 須恵器 甕 (J-34611).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Sue Ware Jar}}{{small|{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} display.}}]] The items excavated during the 1938 excavation (13th year of the Showa era) are as follows{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The manual excavation items were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} through Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture, while the items unearthed by the survey team were transferred to and preserved at {{ill|Kokugakuin University|en|Kokugakuin University|WD=Q495330|lt=Kokugakuin University}}; the collections at both the Tokyo National Museum and the Kokugakuin University Museum are labeled with T and K respectively{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * Decorated Sword ** Bronze‐adorned Double Dragon Ring‐Headed Sword, 1 (T) ** Bronze‐adorned Sword, 1 (location unknown) ** Silver‐adorned Twisted Ring‐Headed Sword Hilt, 1 (T) ** Bronze‐made Sword Scabbard Ornament Fragment, collectively (T) ** Skull‐shaped Sword Hilt, 1 (location unknown) * Weapons ** Straight Sword, 2 or more (T) – possibly the blade portion of the bronze scabbard ornament fragment ** Iron halberd shaft and stone tip (K) ** Silver‐made dagger (possibly K) ** Iron arrowheads (T, K) * Ornaments ** Bronze‐made Double Fish‐shaped Pendant, 1 pair (T) ** Bronze‐made Glass Bead‐attached Leaf‐shaped Waist Ornament, 1 pair (K) ** Bronze‐made Square Floral‐shaped Ornaments, 9 (K) ** Small glass beads – possibly from the leaf‐shaped waist ornament * Horse Fittings ** Bronze‐made Heart‐shaped Apricot Leaf with hinge, 2 (T) ** Bronze‐adorned saddle and stirrup fittings, 3 sets (T1, K2) ** Bronze‐made remnants of a covered wheel, 6 (T) ** Incomplete iron spurred stirrup, 1 pair (T) ** Iron‐based bronze leather fastening fittings, 6 (T) * Bronze bowl, 1 (K) * {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} – 3 broken lids, 3 or more broken bodies; 5 high broken jars with lids, 4 high broken jars with lids, 2 high broken jars without lids, 2 long‐necked jars with feet, 1 long‐necked jar with lid, 1 footed crucible, 1 jar (all T) * {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}} – 1 broken vessel, 3 jars (all T) == Tsukanokoshi Kofun == {{Japanese Kofun |name = Tsukanokoshi Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukanokoshi Kofun (Kisarazu), gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Vicinity of the site |alternate_name = Tsukanokoshi Kofun |part_of = {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}} |location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|Kisarazu|en|Kisarazu|WD=Q335427|lt=Kisarazu City}} Asahi 2‐chome |coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|3.00|N|139|56|1.00|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline|name=塚の腰古墳}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_size = 39.5 m on each side |burial = Unknown |excavations = Bronze mirror, straight sword, iron arrowheads, horse fittings, {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, among others |Attached mound = |built = First half of the {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} |Interred = |Mausoleum = |Historic Site = None |Tangible Cultural Property = |notes = The tumulus is no longer extant }} '''Tsukanokoshi Kofun''' (塚の腰古墳) was a Kofun located to the south of Matsumen Kofun. Its type was that of a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. It was one of the kofun comprising the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}. The tumulus is now lost. == Overview == It is a large square kofun constructed to the south of Matsumen Kofun, separated by a large moat (Moat No.2). It was excavated in {{ill|1909|en|1909|WD=Q2057|lt=1909}} (42nd year of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}), during which burial goods were unearthed, and further excavation surveys were conducted in the fiscal years of {{ill|2005|en|2005|WD=Q2019|lt=2005}}, {{ill|2010|en|2010|WD=Q1995|lt=2010}}, and {{ill|2014|en|2014|WD=Q1999|lt=2014}} (17th, 22nd, and 26th fiscal years of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}). The tumulus was square in type (previously considered a small circular mound before investigation), with each side measuring approximately 39.5 meters. Around the mound were both a peripheral moat and an outer moat; including the peripheral moat, the overall map_size was about 61.0 meters, and including the outer moat, about 73.5 meters{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. As the burial facility has been lost, its details remain unknown{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The 1909 excavation (42nd year of the Meiji era) unearthed burial goods including a bronze mirror, a straight sword, iron arrowheads, horse fittings, and {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, among others. The construction period is estimated to be in the first half of the {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} (TK217 period) of the Late Kofun period. Within the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}, it is assumed to be a chieftain tomb succeeding Matsumen Kofun{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. === Excavated Items === [[File:塚の腰古墳 出土品.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Excavated Items}}{{small|Displayed at {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|1=Kisarazu Hometown Museum Kin-no-Suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91380712}}.}}]] The burial goods from the 1909 excavation (42nd year of the Meiji era) are as follows{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}: * Replica Four‐Animal Mirror, 1 – Diameter 10.75 cm, missing about one–third; similar to the mirror unearthed from Toriya‐baja Kofun No.1 (in Iida, Nagano Prefecture) * Bronze‐made Saddle and Stirrup Fitting, 1 * Straight Sword, 1 * Amber Bead, 1 * Small Glass Beads, 2 * {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} – 1 long–necked jar According to Nagasuka Local History, iron arrowheads are also believed to have been unearthed{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Of the above items, all except the straight sword and iron arrowheads were retained by the landowner, then passed to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum, and are now preserved at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|1=Kisarazu Hometown Museum Kin-no-Suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91380712}}{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|1=Kisarazu Hometown Museum Kin-no-Suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91380712}} (Ōta, Kisarazu City) – Preserves the burial goods from Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} (Taitō, Tokyo) – Preserves the burial goods from Matsumen Kofun. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokugakuin University Museum|1=Kokugakuin University Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q81916990}} (Higashi, Shibuya, Tokyo; located within the Kokugakuin University Shibuya Campus) – Preserves the burial goods from Matsumen Kofun (not on permanent display). == Footnotes == {{reflist}} == References == {{small|(Sources used for writing this article)}} * {{Cite book|Japanese book|editor=|author=小沢洋|year=1989|chapter=Matsumen Kofun|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Matsumen Kofun (古墳)|1989}}}} (平凡社)|1996}}}} * {{Cite book|Japanese book|author=|year=2003|chapter=Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|title=History of Chiba Prefecture: Materials Edition, Archaeology 2 (Prefectural History Series Vicinity of the site |alternate_name = Former Shinchi Kofun |part_of = {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}} |location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|Kisarazu|en|Kisarazu|WD=Q335427|lt=Kisarazu City}} Asahi 2‐chome |coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=松面古墳}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_size = 44.2m×45.3m |burial = Two‐sleeve style {{ill|Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} |excavations = {{ill|Decorated Sword|ja|装飾付大刀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decorated Sword|1=decorated swords|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48749737}} and numerous other burial goods, {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}}, and {{ill|Shura|ja|修羅 (そり)|lt=Shura|lt_ja=修羅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shura|1=Shura (sled)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11386350}} |Attached mound = |built = Early {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} |Interred = |Mausoleum = |Historic Site = None |Tangible Cultural Property = |notes = Ranked as the third‐largest square kofun in Chiba Prefecture
The tumulus is no longer extant |map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=Square Kofun.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a Kofun (kofun) located in Asahi, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|Kisarazu|en|Kisarazu|WD=Q335427|lt=Kisarazu City}}. Its type was that of a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. It was one of the kofun comprising the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}. The tumulus is now lost. In this article the mound located to the south of Matsumen Kofun – '''{{ill|Matsumen Kofun|lt=Matsumen Kofun|lt=Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 松面古墳}}''' – is also explained. == Overview == It is a large square kofun built on the alluvial plain along the left bank of the lower reaches of the {{ill|Obitsu River|en|Obitsu River|WD=Q7074982|lt=Kobiki River}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To the south, separated by a large moat (Moat No.2), stood the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. In {{ill|1938|en|1938|WD=Q18645|lt=1938}} (the 13th year of the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Showa era}}), its stone chamber was excavated and investigated and burial goods were unearthed; later, after being leveled and becoming a buried mound, excavation surveys were carried out in {{ill|2005|en|2005|WD=Q2019|lt=2005}}, {{ill|2010|en|2010|WD=Q1995|lt=2010}}, and {{ill|2014|en|2014|WD=Q1999|lt=2014}} (in the 17th, 22nd, and 26th fiscal years of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}). The tumulus was square in type (previously regarded as a small circular mound before investigation), measuring 44.2 meters east–west and 45.3 meters north–south – making it the third largest square kofun in Chiba Prefecture{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Around the mound, both a peripheral moat and an outer moat encircled the site; including the peripheral moat, the overall map_size was approximately 69.5 meters, and including the outer moat, about 84.5 meters{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. From the peripheral moat were unearthed wooden objects – such as plowshares, handles, stakes, {{ill|Shura|ja|修羅 (そり)|lt=Shura|lt_ja=修羅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shura|1=Shura (sled)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11386350}}, and sword‐like items – and notably the Shura, used for transporting stone during construction, is noteworthy as only the second example in the country after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitsuzuka Kofun|qq=}} (in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}/{{ill|Fujiidera|en|Fujiidera|WD=Q634011|lt=Fujiidera City}}). The burial facility was the two‐sleeve style {{ill|Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}. Its stone chamber was constructed from cut soft sandstone with a flagstone floor, according to reports{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Although there is a possibility that a Sarcophagus passed on to a hospital was used, no other records mention this, leaving it unclear{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The 1938 excavation (13th year of the Showa era) unearthed numerous burial goods from within the stone chamber – including the {{ill|Decorated Sword|ja|装飾付大刀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decorated Sword|1=decorated swords|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48749737}}, various weapons, ornaments, horse fittings, {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, and {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}}. The construction period is estimated to be in the early {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} (TK209 period) of the Late Kofun period{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Within the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}, it is thought to have succeeded the {{ill|Kanazurizuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳|1=Kinreizuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanazurizuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinreizuka Kofun|qq=}} (in {{ill|Kisarazu City Nagasuka|ja|木更津市長須賀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Nagasuka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) and is assumed to be a chieftain tomb preceding the Tsukanokoshi Kofun – making it one of the representative Late Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == Archaeological History == * In {{ill|1909|en|1909|WD=Q2057|lt=1909}} (42nd year of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}), the Tsukanokoshi Kofun was excavated during land reclamation (or soil removal for a prefectural road) – as recorded in the Chiba Prefecture Kunitsu County Gazette (Volume 1), Nagasuka Local History, and Kisarazu City History{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. ** excavations: After being retained by the landowner, all items except for the straight sword were donated in {{ill|1972|en|1972|WD=Q2476|lt=1972}} (47th year of the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Showa era}}) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum, and are now preserved at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|1=Kisarazu Hometown Museum Kin-no-Suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91380712}}{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In {{ill|1938|en|1938|WD=Q18645|lt=1938}} (13th year of the Showa era), an emergency survey of the Matsumen Kofun was conducted in connection with the construction of the former Kunitsu Hospital; the site was leveled after the survey (by the Suga Archaeological Survey Group){{Sfn|祇園・長須賀古墳群（千葉県の歴史 資料編 考古2）|2003}}. ** The manual excavation on June 29 – the burial goods were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} through Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. ** The items excavated during the survey on July 19–20 were transferred to and preserved at {{ill|Kokugakuin University|en|Kokugakuin University|WD=Q495330|lt=Kokugakuin University}}{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In the fiscal year of {{ill|2005|en|2005|WD=Q2019|lt=2005}} (17th fiscal year of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}), a verification survey of Matsumen Kofun was conducted in connection with soil improvement and the removal of buried objects (by the Kisarazu City Board of Education, reported in {{ill|2006|en|2006|WD=Q2021|lt=2006}}){{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In the fiscal year of {{ill|2010|en|2010|WD=Q1995|lt=2010}} (22nd fiscal year of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}), a verification survey of both Matsumen Kofun and Tsukanokoshi Kofun was carried out in connection with soil improvement and the removal of buried objects (by the Kisarazu City Board of Education, reported in {{ill|2013|en|2013|WD=Q1998|lt=2013}}){{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In the fiscal year of {{ill|2014|en|2014|WD=Q1999|lt=2014}} (26th fiscal year of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}), a full-map_size survey of both Matsumen Kofun and Tsukanokoshi Kofun was conducted in connection with soil improvement and the removal of buried objects (by the Kisarazu City Board of Education, with the report published in {{ill|2016|en|2016|WD=Q25245|lt=2016}}){{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. == Excavated Items == [[File:松面古墳出土 [[File:松面古墳出土 金銅製魚佩 (J-34624).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Bronze Fish‐shaped Ornament}}{{small|{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} display.}}]] [[File:松面古墳出土 須恵器 甕 (J-34611).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Sue Ware Jar}}{{small|{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} display.}}]] The items excavated during the 1938 excavation (13th year of the Showa era) are as follows{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The manual excavation items were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} through Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture, while the items unearthed by the survey team were transferred to and preserved at {{ill|Kokugakuin University|en|Kokugakuin University|WD=Q495330|lt=Kokugakuin University}}; the collections at both the Tokyo National Museum and the Kokugakuin University Museum are labeled with T and K respectively{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * Decorated Sword ** Bronze‐adorned Double Dragon Ring‐Headed Sword, 1 (T) ** Bronze‐adorned Sword, 1 (location unknown) ** Silver‐adorned Twisted Ring‐Headed Sword Hilt, 1 (T) ** Bronze‐made Sword Scabbard Ornament Fragment, collectively (T) ** Skull‐shaped Sword Hilt, 1 (location unknown) * Weapons ** Straight Sword, 2 or more (T) – possibly the blade portion of the bronze scabbard ornament fragment ** Iron halberd shaft and stone tip (K) ** Silver‐made dagger (possibly K) ** Iron arrowheads (T, K) * Ornaments ** Bronze‐made Double Fish‐shaped Pendant, 1 pair (T) ** Bronze‐made Glass Bead‐attached Leaf‐shaped Waist Ornament, 1 pair (K) ** Bronze‐made Square Floral‐shaped Ornaments, 9 (K) ** Small glass beads – possibly from the leaf‐shaped waist ornament * Horse Fittings ** Bronze‐made Heart‐shaped Apricot Leaf with hinge, 2 (T) ** Bronze‐adorned saddle and stirrup fittings, 3 sets (T1, K2) ** Bronze‐made remnants of a covered wheel, 6 (T) ** Incomplete iron spurred stirrup, 1 pair (T) ** Iron‐based bronze leather fastening fittings, 6 (T) * Bronze bowl, 1 (K) * {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} – 3 broken lids, 3 or more broken bodies; 5 high broken jars with lids, 4 high broken jars with lids, 2 high broken jars without lids, 2 long‐necked jars with feet, 1 long‐necked jar with lid, 1 footed crucible, 1 jar (all T) * {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}} – 1 broken vessel, 3 jars (all T) == Tsukanokoshi Kofun == {{Japanese Kofun |name = Tsukanokoshi Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukanokoshi Kofun (Kisarazu), gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Vicinity of the site |alternate_name = Tsukanokoshi Kofun |part_of = {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}} |location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|Kisarazu|en|Kisarazu|WD=Q335427|lt=Kisarazu City}} Asahi 2‐chome |coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|3.00|N|139|56|1.00|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline|name=塚の腰古墳}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_size = 39.5 m on each side |burial = Unknown |excavations = Bronze mirror, straight sword, iron arrowheads, horse fittings, {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, among others |Attached mound = |built = First half of the {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} |Interred = |Mausoleum = |Historic Site = None |Tangible Cultural Property = |notes = The tumulus is no longer extant }} '''Tsukanokoshi Kofun''' (塚の腰古墳) was a Kofun located to the south of Matsumen Kofun. Its type was that of a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. It was one of the kofun comprising the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}. The tumulus is now lost. == Overview == It is a large square kofun constructed to the south of Matsumen Kofun, separated by a large moat (Moat No.2). It was excavated in {{ill|1909|en|1909|WD=Q2057|lt=1909}} (42nd year of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}), during which burial goods were unearthed, and further excavation surveys were conducted in the fiscal years of {{ill|2005|en|2005|WD=Q2019|lt=2005}}, {{ill|2010|en|2010|WD=Q1995|lt=2010}}, and {{ill|2014|en|2014|WD=Q1999|lt=2014}} (17th, 22nd, and 26th fiscal years of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}). The tumulus was square in type (previously considered a small circular mound before investigation), with each side measuring approximately 39.5 meters. Around the mound were both a peripheral moat and an outer moat; including the peripheral moat, the overall map_size was about 61.0 meters, and including the outer moat, about 73.5 meters{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. As the burial facility has been lost, its details remain unknown{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The 1909 excavation (42nd year of the Meiji era) unearthed burial goods including a bronze mirror, a straight sword, iron arrowheads, horse fittings, and {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, among others. The construction period is estimated to be in the first half of the {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} (TK217 period) of the Late Kofun period. Within the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}, it is assumed to be a chieftain tomb succeeding Matsumen Kofun{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. === Excavated Items === [[File:塚の腰古墳 出土品.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Excavated Items}}{{small|Displayed at {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|1=Kisarazu Hometown Museum Kin-no-Suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91380712}}.}}]] The burial goods from the 1909 excavation (42nd year of the Meiji era) are as follows{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}: * Replica Four‐Animal Mirror, 1 – Diameter 10.75 cm, missing about one–third; similar to the mirror unearthed from Toriya‐baja Kofun No.1 (in Iida, Nagano Prefecture) * Bronze‐made Saddle and Stirrup Fitting, 1 * Straight Sword, 1 * Amber Bead, 1 * Small Glass Beads, 2 * {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} – 1 long–necked jar According to Nagasuka Local History, iron arrowheads are also believed to have been unearthed{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Of the above items, all except the straight sword and iron arrowheads were retained by the landowner, then passed to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum, and are now preserved at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|1=Kisarazu Hometown Museum Kin-no-Suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91380712}}{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|1=Kisarazu Hometown Museum Kin-no-Suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91380712}} (Ōta, Kisarazu City) – Preserves the burial goods from Tsukanokoshi Kofun. * {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} (Taitō, Tokyo) – Preserves the burial goods from Matsumen Kofun. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokugakuin University Museum|1=Kokugakuin University Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q81916990}} (Higashi, Shibuya, Tokyo; located [[ja:松面古墳]] [[ja:松面古墳]] [[ja:松面古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site|coordinates={{Coord|35.38505555555555|N|139.93347222222224|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}}} {{Japanese Kofun |name = Matsumen Kofun |image = [[File:Matsumen Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Vicinity of the site |alternate_name = Former Shinchi Kofun |part_of = {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}} |location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|Kisarazu|en|Kisarazu|WD=Q335427|lt=Kisarazu City}} Asahi 2‐chome |coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|6.20|N|139|56|0.45|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=松面古墳}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_size = 44.2m×45.3m |burial = Two‐sleeve style {{ill|Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} |excavations = {{ill|Decorated Sword|ja|装飾付大刀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decorated Sword|1=decorated swords|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48749737}} and numerous other burial goods, {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}}, and {{ill|Shura|ja|修羅 (そり)|lt=Shura|lt_ja=修羅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shura|1=Shura (sled)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11386350}} |Attached mound = |built = Early {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} |Interred = |Mausoleum = |Historic Site = None |Tangible Cultural Property = |notes = Ranked as the third‐largest square kofun in Chiba Prefecture
The tumulus is no longer extant |map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|label=Matsumen Kofun|lat_deg=35|lat_min=23|lat_sec=6.20|lon_deg=139|lon_min=56|lon_sec=0.45|mark=Square Kofun.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Matsumen Kofun''' (松面古墳) was a Kofun (kofun) located in Asahi, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|Kisarazu|en|Kisarazu|WD=Q335427|lt=Kisarazu City}}. Its type was that of a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. It was one of the kofun comprising the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}. The tumulus is now lost. In this article the mound located to the south of Matsumen Kofun – '''{{ill|Matsumen Kofun|lt=Matsumen Kofun|lt=Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja|塚の腰古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukanokoshi Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 松面古墳}}''' – is also explained. == Overview == It is a large square kofun built on the alluvial plain along the left bank of the lower reaches of the {{ill|Obitsu River|en|Obitsu River|WD=Q7074982|lt=Kobiki River}} in central Chiba Prefecture. To the south, separated by a large moat (Moat No.2), stood the Tsukanokoshi Kofun. In {{ill|1938|en|1938|WD=Q18645|lt=1938}} (the 13th year of the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Showa era}}), its stone chamber was excavated and investigated and burial goods were unearthed; later, after being leveled and becoming a buried mound, excavation surveys were carried out in {{ill|2005|en|2005|WD=Q2019|lt=2005}}, {{ill|2010|en|2010|WD=Q1995|lt=2010}}, and {{ill|2014|en|2014|WD=Q1999|lt=2014}} (in the 17th, 22nd, and 26th fiscal years of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}). The tumulus was square in type (previously regarded as a small circular mound before investigation), measuring 44.2 meters east–west and 45.3 meters north–south – making it the third largest square kofun in Chiba Prefecture{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Around the mound, both a peripheral moat and an outer moat encircled the site; including the peripheral moat, the overall map_size was approximately 69.5 meters, and including the outer moat, about 84.5 meters{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. From the peripheral moat were unearthed wooden objects – such as plowshares, handles, stakes, {{ill|Shura|ja|修羅 (そり)|lt=Shura|lt_ja=修羅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shura|1=Shura (sled)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11386350}}, and sword‐like items – and notably the Shura, used for transporting stone during construction, is noteworthy as only the second example in the country after the {{ill|Mitsuzuka Kofun|ja|三ツ塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitsuzuka Kofun|qq=}} (in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}/{{ill|Fujiidera|en|Fujiidera|WD=Q634011|lt=Fujiidera City}}). The burial facility was the two‐sleeve style {{ill|Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Horizontal tunnel‐style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}. Its stone chamber was constructed from cut soft sandstone with a flagstone floor, according to reports{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Although there is a possibility that a Sarcophagus passed on to a hospital was used, no other records mention this, leaving it unclear{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The 1938 excavation (13th year of the Showa era) unearthed numerous burial goods from within the stone chamber – including the {{ill|Decorated Sword|ja|装飾付大刀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decorated Sword|1=decorated swords|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48749737}}, various weapons, ornaments, horse fittings, {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, and {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}}. The construction period is estimated to be in the early {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} (TK209 period) of the Late Kofun period{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Within the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}, it is thought to have succeeded the {{ill|Kanazurizuka Kofun|ja|金鈴塚古墳|1=Kinreizuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanazurizuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinreizuka Kofun|qq=}} (in {{ill|Kisarazu City Nagasuka|ja|木更津市長須賀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Nagasuka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) and is assumed to be a chieftain tomb preceding the Tsukanokoshi Kofun – making it one of the representative Late Kofun period tombs in the Bōsō region. == Archaeological History == * In {{ill|1909|en|1909|WD=Q2057|lt=1909}} (42nd year of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}), the Tsukanokoshi Kofun was excavated during land reclamation (or soil removal for a prefectural road) – as recorded in the Chiba Prefecture Kunitsu County Gazette (Volume 1), Nagasuka Local History, and Kisarazu City History{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. ** excavations: After being retained by the landowner, all items except for the straight sword were donated in {{ill|1972|en|1972|WD=Q2476|lt=1972}} (47th year of the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Showa era}}) to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum, and are now preserved at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|1=Kisarazu Hometown Museum Kin-no-Suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91380712}}{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In {{ill|1938|en|1938|WD=Q18645|lt=1938}} (13th year of the Showa era), an emergency survey of the Matsumen Kofun was conducted in connection with the construction of the former Kunitsu Hospital; the site was leveled after the survey (by the Suga Archaeological Survey Group){{Sfn|祇園・長須賀古墳群（千葉県の歴史 資料編 考古2）|2003}}. ** The manual excavation on June 29 – the burial goods were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} through Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. ** The items excavated during the survey on July 19–20 were transferred to and preserved at {{ill|Kokugakuin University|en|Kokugakuin University|WD=Q495330|lt=Kokugakuin University}}{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In the fiscal year of {{ill|2005|en|2005|WD=Q2019|lt=2005}} (17th fiscal year of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}), a verification survey of Matsumen Kofun was conducted in connection with soil improvement and the removal of buried objects (by the Kisarazu City Board of Education, reported in {{ill|2006|en|2006|WD=Q2021|lt=2006}}){{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In the fiscal year of {{ill|2010|en|2010|WD=Q1995|lt=2010}} (22nd fiscal year of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}), a verification survey of both Matsumen Kofun and Tsukanokoshi Kofun was carried out in connection with soil improvement and the removal of buried objects (by the Kisarazu City Board of Education, reported in {{ill|2013|en|2013|WD=Q1998|lt=2013}}){{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * In the fiscal year of {{ill|2014|en|2014|WD=Q1999|lt=2014}} (26th fiscal year of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}), a full-map_size survey of both Matsumen Kofun and Tsukanokoshi Kofun was conducted in connection with soil improvement and the removal of buried objects (by the Kisarazu City Board of Education, with the report published in {{ill|2016|en|2016|WD=Q25245|lt=2016}}){{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. == Excavated Items == [[File:松面古墳出土 双龍環頭大刀 (J-34620).JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Double Dragon Ring‐Headed Sword}}{{small|{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} display.}}]] [[File:松面古墳出土 金銅製魚佩 (J-34624).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Bronze Fish‐shaped Ornament}}{{small|{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} display.}}]] [[File:松面古墳出土 須恵器 甕 (J-34611).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Sue Ware Jar}}{{small|{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} display.}}]] The items excavated during the 1938 excavation (13th year of the Showa era) are as follows{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The manual excavation items were purchased and preserved by the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} through Kisarazu Police and Chiba Prefecture, while the items unearthed by the survey team were transferred to and preserved at {{ill|Kokugakuin University|en|Kokugakuin University|WD=Q495330|lt=Kokugakuin University}}; the collections at both the Tokyo National Museum and the Kokugakuin University Museum are labeled with T and K respectively{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. * Decorated Sword ** Bronze‐adorned Double Dragon Ring‐Headed Sword, 1 (T) ** Bronze‐adorned Sword, 1 (location unknown) ** Silver‐adorned Twisted Ring‐Headed Sword Hilt, 1 (T) ** Bronze‐made Sword Scabbard Ornament Fragment, collectively (T) ** Skull‐shaped Sword Hilt, 1 (location unknown) * Weapons ** Straight Sword, 2 or more (T) – possibly the blade portion of the bronze scabbard ornament fragment ** Iron halberd shaft and stone tip (K) ** Silver‐made dagger (possibly K) ** Iron arrowheads (T, K) * Ornaments ** Bronze‐made Double Fish‐shaped Pendant, 1 pair (T) ** Bronze‐made Glass Bead‐attached Leaf‐shaped Waist Ornament, 1 pair (K) ** Bronze‐made Square Floral‐shaped Ornaments, 9 (K) ** Small glass beads – possibly from the leaf‐shaped waist ornament * Horse Fittings ** Bronze‐made Heart‐shaped Apricot Leaf with hinge, 2 (T) ** Bronze‐adorned saddle and stirrup fittings, 3 sets (T1, K2) ** Bronze‐made remnants of a covered wheel, 6 (T) ** Incomplete iron spurred stirrup, 1 pair (T) ** Iron‐based bronze leather fastening fittings, 6 (T) * Bronze bowl, 1 (K) * {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} – 3 broken lids, 3 or more broken bodies; 5 high broken jars with lids, 4 high broken jars with lids, 2 high broken jars without lids, 2 long‐necked jars with feet, 1 long‐necked jar with lid, 1 footed crucible, 1 jar (all T) * {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}} – 1 broken vessel, 3 jars (all T) == Tsukanokoshi Kofun == {{Japanese Kofun |name = Tsukanokoshi Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukanokoshi Kofun (Kisarazu), gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Vicinity of the site |alternate_name = Tsukanokoshi Kofun |part_of = {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}} |location = {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|Kisarazu|en|Kisarazu|WD=Q335427|lt=Kisarazu City}} Asahi 2‐chome |coordinates = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|23|3.00|N|139|56|1.00|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline|name=塚の腰古墳}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_size = 39.5 m on each side |burial = Unknown |excavations = Bronze mirror, straight sword, iron arrowheads, horse fittings, {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, among others |Attached mound = |built = First half of the {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} |Interred = |Mausoleum = |Historic Site = None |Tangible Cultural Property = |notes = The tumulus is no longer extant }} '''Tsukanokoshi Kofun''' (塚の腰古墳) was a Kofun located to the south of Matsumen Kofun. Its type was that of a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. It was one of the kofun comprising the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}. The tumulus is now lost. == Overview == It is a large square kofun constructed to the south of Matsumen Kofun, separated by a large moat (Moat No.2). It was excavated in {{ill|1909|en|1909|WD=Q2057|lt=1909}} (42nd year of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}), during which burial goods were unearthed, and further excavation surveys were conducted in the fiscal years of {{ill|2005|en|2005|WD=Q2019|lt=2005}}, {{ill|2010|en|2010|WD=Q1995|lt=2010}}, and {{ill|2014|en|2014|WD=Q1999|lt=2014}} (17th, 22nd, and 26th fiscal years of the {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei era}}). The tumulus was square in type (previously considered a small circular mound before investigation), with each side measuring approximately 39.5 meters. Around the mound were both a peripheral moat and an outer moat; including the peripheral moat, the overall map_size was about 61.0 meters, and including the outer moat, about 73.5 meters{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. As the burial facility has been lost, its details remain unknown{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. The 1909 excavation (42nd year of the Meiji era) unearthed burial goods including a bronze mirror, a straight sword, iron arrowheads, horse fittings, and {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}}, among others. The construction period is estimated to be in the first half of the {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} (TK217 period) of the Late Kofun period. Within the {{ill|Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|ja|祇園・長須賀古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion‐Nagasuka Kofun Group|qq=}}, it is assumed to be a chieftain tomb succeeding Matsumen Kofun{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. === Excavated Items === [[File:塚の腰古墳 出土品.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Excavated Items}}{{small|Displayed at {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|1=Kisarazu Hometown Museum Kin-no-Suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91380712}}.}}]] The burial goods from the 1909 excavation (42nd year of the Meiji era) are as follows{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}: * Replica Four‐Animal Mirror, 1 – Diameter 10.75 cm, missing about one–third; similar to the mirror unearthed from Toriya‐baja Kofun No.1 (in Iida, Nagano Prefecture) * Bronze‐made Saddle and Stirrup Fitting, 1 * Straight Sword, 1 * Amber Bead, 1 * Small Glass Beads, 2 * {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} – 1 long–necked jar According to Nagasuka Local History, iron arrowheads are also believed to have been unearthed{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. Of the above items, all except the straight sword and iron arrowheads were retained by the landowner, then passed to the Chiba Prefectural Kazusa Museum, and are now preserved at the {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|1=Kisarazu Hometown Museum Kin-no-Suzu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91380712}}{{Sfn|塚の腰古墳・松面古墳発掘調査報告書|2016}}. == Related Facilities == * {{ill|Kisarazu City Local Museum Kanenosuzu|ja|木更津市郷土博物館金のすず|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kisarazu City Local Museum National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}} (Taitō, Tokyo) – Preserves the burial goods from Matsumen Kofun. * {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokugakuin University Museum|1=Kokugakuin University Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q81916990}} (Higashi, Shibuya, Tokyo; located within the Kokugakuin University Shibuya Campus) – Preserves the burial goods from Matsumen Kofun (not on permanent display). == Footnotes == {{reflist}} == References == {{small|(Sources used for
